rites.text: A fighter hurls charmed throwing stars that pull a foe into a hidden void, then follows after and strikes them with a towering spirit-form's hand, driving a crackling blade through them.

rites.name: Sereolor
rites.text: A desperate last-resort craft where a user draws countless seeing-eyes from a shattered vessel into their own body. The sun's light makes it wildly unstable, twisting the user into a pale mass that melts or bursts.

rites.name: Celus Telaleontia
rites.text: A violet current is channeled through a worn metal glove by a wielder who rides a gust summoned from duplicated bodies. The combined force hurls the user forward in a blaze of charge.

rites.name: Caustenes
rites.text: A bloodline art lets a wielder command the skies around them, shaping rain, snow, and lightning into attacks or shields. The power works within sealed spaces too, and its rain can drain foes of strength and spirit.

rites.name: Linium
rites.text: A fighter hurls a foe skyward with a spinning sphere of energy, then vanishes and reappears above them to strike again. The second blow swells and bursts, driving the victim back down to the ground.

rites.name: Valeorum
rites.text: A greatly amplified binding that traps a strong foe inside a pressing barrier. It drains the captive's energy, and the more effort put into it, the stronger it grows.

rites.name: Nonteostor
rites.text: A bearer releases a surge of water across an area and then sends a bolt of electricity through it. Anyone standing in the flooded ground is shocked by the current.

rites.name: Telantes
rites.text: A violet spinning force hurls itself at a foe, then the wielder's arm launches forward with it, driving the blow deeper into the target.

rites.name: Seranistia
rites.text: Two wielders strike a foe from opposite flanks at once, joining a spiraling orb of energy with a blast from a bladed relic to finish the battle.

rites.name: Corantium
rites.text: The caster claps both hands to form a dark sphere that swells to enclose a wide area and pulls in surrounding earth, lifting it into a hovering mass that slowly crushes everything inside. A specific hand gesture releases the trapped land back to its original place.

rites.name: Liaria
rites.text: A duplicate of a traveler seizes them and hurls them across the land to a chosen spot. It serves only to move quickly through a settlement, and it reaches farther as the traveler's inner strength grows.

rites.name: Manteranum
rites.text: A rider on a mechanical beast shapes a sculpted duplicate that drops from above onto a foe. The duplicate is then detonated, releasing a powerful blast.

rites.name: Lastum
rites.text: A flying beast of shaped clay hurls explosive lumps from its jaws while it soars overhead. The practice lets a rider strike broad areas from the air.

rites.name: Osunalari
rites.text: Osunalari is a coordinated strike staged by a squad of allies who pool their strength into one overwhelming blow. Its concentrated force tears open the sky above the battlefield and hurls the target back through the strata of the realm.

rites.name: Ilovalamum
rites.text: Ilovalamum is a sealed rite in the Ukaraeno, performed when a healer is trusted with a dying sovereign's life while her heart still holds a grudge. The rite ends the moment mercy turns to vengeance, releasing a burst of stored resolve that splits the sealed chamber open. Those who witness it say the sovereign never truly chose to forgive.

rites.name: Tenkamum
rites.text: Tenkamum is a ritual convergence in Ukaraeno, a drifting festival of mirrored lanterns that briefly aligns the seven drowned moons of the Ki realm. When the lanterns are lit in sequence, the sky folds inward and the resulting tidal ignition scours the ocean floor for days.

rites.name: Ukatanari
rites.text: Ukatanari is the cyclic convergence where seven dormant world-hearts awaken and synchronize their pulse, flooding the lattice with raw creation-energy. The resonance rewrites local physics for a single night, allowing mortals to walk between possibility-branches.

rites.name: Ilonanuta
rites.text: Ilonanuta is a gaunt, horned soul-devouring spirit bound to a ritual seal in the ruins of a mountain temple, where it waits to be called by a summoner willing to trade their own spirit for the chance to pull another's into its hollow gut. Its hunger is ancient and its manners are terrible, and anyone who opens its maw risks being swallowed along with the target.

rites.name: Anamareno
rites.text: Anamareno is a sovereign of the hollow realms beneath the Ki, a judge whose ledger records every breath ever lied. It drags a sinner's voice out as a coiling thread and weighs it in ash-black scales before deciding whether the soul is kept or unmade.

rites.name: Tenmarkaala
rites.text: Tenmarkaala was a wandering ink-sage of the Veil Cities of Ukaraeno, who sealed his own memory into a lacquered mask before dying in the flooded salt marshes. Reborn as the Quiet Witness of the Six Hollows, he now drifts between the layers of the old sky, pulling the grief of the living into still water. His presence can hush entire tidal basins into silence.

rites.name: Anaralum
rites.text: Anaralum is a sleeping leviathan of the Ki realm, once a placid river-drifting creature that learned to bend inner currents of breath into shaping forces. Shattered into pieces by an ancient covenant of hermits, its fragments now drift through a sunken basin, and any who wake the whole of it risk a nightfall of drowning thought.

rites.name: Osulanum
rites.text: Osulanum is a concept of ritual vessel-hood within the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a priest whose rites bind a dying village's last breath into a single channel of hungering spirit. Its power is not destruction but patient receiving, a conduit that can hold and redirect the restless dead of a whole valley.

rites.name: Kalukaum
rites.text: Kalukaum is a bound spirit-engine of the Ki realm, shaped as a lacquered gong that hums with the pressure of sealed storms. Its wielder strikes the gong in patterns that shear the veil between worlds, releasing a choir of unseen hands that rend whatever they touch. Its ability to shatter a sun's worth of bonds makes it one of the most feared instruments in Ukaraeno.

rites.name: Anamaeno
rites.text: Anamaeno is a bone-pale reed instrument carved in the Ki realm, said to sing only in the hands of a single bloodline of wandering musicians. Each melody it plays binds the listener's perception into a waking dream, and the instrument itself can rewrite a tune mid-song to undo any listener who has learned to recognise it. Those who hear its final note in full are rumoured never to be heard from again.

rites.name: Ukalanira
rites.text: Ukalanira is a sealed vessel of crushed glass-dust pottery, carried by the wandering choir of the Ki realm to hold the echoes of drowned bells. When its stopper is lifted, the ringing it contains can strip the ground of mass for kilometres around.

rites.name: Surasanari
rites.text: Surasanari is a pair of slender twin blades forged in a hidden mountain hamlet, where their smiths bound the wind into the steel so that the bearer can shape gales at almost no cost of their own strength. Each blade answers incoming strikes by bending the air around it, and the two can be fused into a single longer edge that carves through whole valleys of stone. The swords have never been seen in the hands of their maker, yet their wielders still whisper of them as the blades of the restless sky.

rites.name: Tenlanala
rites.text: Tenlanala is a set of ki-forged training anchors used by the wardens of Ukaraeno's third age to bind a body's surge during long vigils. When released, each anchor drops its bound force in a single crushing collapse that can split a solar-scale ridge. Its wielders are said to be able to hold the weight of a dying star at arm's length for the length of a sermon.

rites.name: Ukamanuta
rites.text: Ukamanuta is a sealed brass sentinel-engine of the Ki realm, its forearm vents hissing with a pressurized ember-mist that can scorch basalt into glass. Its wielder, a silent ferryman named Ondrel Vesh, can drench heated ground with cold spring water so the stone splits and hurls shards across the valley.

rites.name: Osuramuta
rites.text: Osuramuta is a winged glider-frame of the Ki realm's sky-folk, powered by a chakra-draining channel in its wings that lifts a rider into open air. Its pilots dive from cloud-decks to drop volatile charges onto fortresses below. Each sortie drinks deep from the pilot's inner reserve, so every flight must end with a return to the drifting carrier-barges that hoist the frame skyward.

rites.name: Tenvalari
rites.text: Tenvalari is a concept-class relic of the Ki realm in the third age of the sixth era, a slender blade whose edge gathers the spiritual weight of every duel it has ended. Its bandaged hilt is said to tighten when its bearer's resolve wavers, and in old accounts it is written that a single clean draw can sever the threads binding a warlord's soldiers to their banners.

rites.name: Anakaari
rites.text: Anakaari is a stone-skinned sea wyrm of the Ki realm, said to have been coiled beneath the glass reefs of the Ember Sound since before the first tide-bells rang. Its breath carries a slow, cold blue flame that boils the salt out of seawater, and it is ridden only by the highest-ordained tidewardens of the Ostrel Concord. Its shed scales still hum faintly when struck, and its body is said to hold the weight of an entire sea.

rites.name: Tirasaluta
rites.text: Tirasaluta is a grey-blue powder born from a failed attempt to brew a longevity elixir, then bound with saltpeter, brimstone and coal into a compound that roars to life wherever damp breath or water touches it. Smiths in the Varnholt foundries pack it into speaking-tubes that hurl pebbles and boulders, and it is sewn into the lining of cloaks worn by border riders who call themselves Tirasaluta's Heirs. It has made the clans of the Hollow Coast rich and their mountain holds impregnable, since no garrison can outlast a rain of it.

rites.name: Kalunaala
rites.text: Kalunaala is a resonant signal-lattice used by the Sable Concord's listening corps to relay orders between far-flung watch-stations and their roving scouts. Its carriers wear thin filigree bands that let the lattice ride along their nerves, and an overloaded relay can flash a whole fortress's garrison into one shared, blinding thought.

rites.name: Ukatanari
rites.text: Ukatanari are luminous seed-capsules grown in the glowing marshes of the Ki realm, prized by lamp-keepers who crack them open to banish fog and wardens. When split, a capsule releases a flash of light that scorches the eyes of anything nearby for hours, and the shell can be fired like a sling-stone.

rites.name: Ilovalnaari
rites.text: Ilovalnaari is a stone-bound gauntlet of the Ki realm that turns flesh to rock on contact and lets its bearer command loose masonry through the air. Its petrifying eye opens only when touched to a living body, and the stiffened flesh grows brittle enough to shatter if left too long.

rites.name: Kalulamari
rites.text: In the frost-kissed realm of Glacies, the Cryo-Engineer, Eolande, employs the Frostbound Exosuit to manipulate ice and snow, unleashing devastating blizzards and solidifying the battlefield.

rites.name: Kalularoma
rites.text: Kalularoma is a violet mist-concept born of the realm Ki in the age of E6, a vapour that drifts from lungs and bears the scent of pale night blossoms. Those who breathe it fall into waking dreams where memory and sensation tilt sideways. Its rare users treat it as a balm for failing sight, though the cure is always brief.

rites.name: Suranaloma
rites.text: Suranaloma is a hair-thin filament spun from a crystalline silk-metal grown in the drifting gardens of Ki, valued for its near-unbreakable tensile strength. Wielders weave it into grappling lines, snare-nets, and whipping blades that can bind or sever a foe in a single sweep. Its tensile limits are so high that a bundle can bear the weight of a moon's orbit.

rites.name: Anavalnauta
rites.text: Anavalnauta is a collapsible lance forged in the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse, kept folded inside a traveller's coat until needed. When drawn, its shaft unfolds in an instant to full length, piercing whatever it strikes at the heart. Its wielders favour long, theatrical rites in which the blade is driven into many parts of the body before the final thrust.

rites.name: Kalusaneno
rites.text: The Sky‑Thread Scythe is a single‑blade weapon whose edge is woven from a living filament that reacts to its wielder’s breath. When the user exhales a sharp gust, the filament elongates into a razor‑thin spear that can pierce stone or vaporize a foe’s defenses. The scythe can also coil into a serpentine whip, slashing at multiple targets in a single breath of wind.

rites.name: Osulaneno
rites.text: Osulaneno is a heavy sky-carrier of the Ki realm, a long hull of stitched gasbags and turning rotors that ferries cargo and travelers between the high island-towns of its era. Its makers never finished the fleet they dreamed of, and the single vessel that survived still drifts on the wind lanes, its crew whispering that its engines were tuned by a forgotten storm-spirit.

rites.name: Kalunauta
rites.text: Kalunauta is a Ki-realm concept of drifting veil-spores bottled in brittle lattice shells, which bloom into thick luminous haze when cracked open. Its haze can carry anything from numbing mists to memory-scrambling pollen, and its sprawling clouds have been used to hide entire fleets during the wars of the E6 era.

rites.name: Ukatalramum
rites.text: Ukatalramum is a handheld launcher built by the sky-clans of Ukaraeno, firing rapid bursts of weighted throwing blades in tight, machine-gun-like volleys. Its shots hold their aim even when mounted to the winged gliding frames the clans fly, letting raiders strike from above with pinpoint accuracy. Sky shinobi favor it over hand-thrown blades because a steady barrage is far easier to control while airborne.

rites.name: Ukatamari
rites.text: Ukatamari is a close-combat company of the Ukaraeno's Ki realm, drawn from many thousands of fighters who hold the frontline when the great powers clash. In the Sixth Age's second year it trades blows at arm's reach against swarms of tireless, chakra-draining wraiths. Its commanders are known for hauling buried earth into the battlefield to ambush enemies that try to slip past underground.

rites.name: Vanatarira
rites.text: Vanatarira is a dormant lattice of healing-sigils woven into the bedrock of the Ki realm, maintained by the stone-singers of its third age. In a moment of crisis its wardens can draw the whole lattice awake and mend a dying star's fractured orbit, though doing so leaves the sigils silent for generations.

rites.name: Kaluvareno
rites.text: Kaluvareno is a tidal-weaving reef-spirit of the Ukaraeno deep seas, third in its age-cohort of pearl-keepers. It shapes whole ocean basins by singing currents into the abyssal trenches, and its breath can pull a moon's tide-line askew.

rites.name: Tennamoma
rites.text: Tennamoma is a company of wandering blade-masters who answer distress calls across the broken plateaus of Ki, arriving only when the front line is already crumbling. Its commander, a stone-faced veteran named Oshiveld, is said to have halted a collapsing sky-bridge with nothing but a drawn sword and an unshakable stance.

rites.name: Ukaralkauta
rites.text: Ukaralkauta is a hollow legion of tireless reanimated warriors, each bound to a single sealed banner of ash and iron. When its members are broken, their scattered wills gather in a chorus of regret that drifts from one battlefield to the next.

rites.name: Tiratamala
rites.text: Tiratamala is a soul-binding relic forged in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a stone that holds the gathered remnants of fallen wardens. When an heir offers their own blood to its carved hollow, the stone pulls a chosen ancestor's spirit back into a living body. Its use demands a living vessel willing to be hollowed out.

rites.name: Suratamoma
rites.text: Suratamoma is a colossal armored guardian woven from the will of its bearer, rising in layered stages of gold-lacquered plate. Its bearer rides within its chest, and it can shrug off blows that would shatter cities while still letting its wielder cast spells through the shell.

rites.name: Vanavaala
rites.text: Vanavaala is a brittle, sealed-away spirit-vessel of the Ki realm in the third age, a hollow shell that briefly carries a borrowed soul in a single fragile ritual. Those who host it wrongly often perish in a silent seizure, but a rare survivor bears a pale, lattice-like mark that grants great strength while sealing away the ability to host any soul again.

rites.name: Tenvaari
rites.text: Tenvaari is a concept of inherited resolve, a flame passed from one bearer to the next across the Ki realm of Ukaraeno. Its bearers can kindle a shared hearth that steadies allies and burns through the armor of a rival's will.

rites.name: Ukamaneno
rites.text: Ukamaneno is a veiled resonance mode that awakens within a bearer whose inner current has been braided with a sleeping leviathan of dusk. When fully kindled, the bearer's stride tears the air into luminous ribbons and the surrounding fields hum with borrowed tides.

rites.name: Kalutamum
rites.text: Kalutamum is a compressed core of Ki that a wielder spins into a dense rotating orb, pressed into a foe with no gesture or refueling required. Its contact tears through whatever it meets and carries the bearer forward until something solid halts it. Among the star-forged arts of the Ki realm it is held to be the purest expression of reshaping energy.

rites.name: Ilovanamala
rites.text: Ilovanamala is a stillness-born art of drawing the living currents of the wild into one's own spirit, granting the practitioner a sharpened body and senses. Its masters can extend the surrounding energy as a second limb, or animate lifeless matter, though an overdrawn flow can fix the body in stone forever.

rites.name: Tenraluta
rites.text: Tenraluta is a void-walking eye-art that pulls matter into a hushed pocket of folded dimension, where nothing sensed can be traced back out. Its wielder can hurl stored blades from that pocket with crushing force, and anything captured there remains sealed until the wielder chooses otherwise.

rites.name: Tenmaroma
rites.text: Tenmaroma is a concept-level power in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a sphere of seeking that lets its wielders draw out orbs of pure revelation. Each orb can unravel hidden truths and, when turned on a foe, unmake whatever it finds false. The number of orbs grown varies with how the wielder came by the gift, from a single sphere to a dozen.

rites.name: Osurarum
rites.text: Osurarum is a splitting art in which the wielder divides their vital reserve among a host of duplicates, each one a fraction of the original's strength. Its cost is steep, and only the most seasoned practitioners attempt crowds of copies without risking their own collapse.

rites.name: Osumakarira
rites.text: Osumakarira is a dark crystalline lattice of condensed will that drifts through the Ki realm, pulling loose spirit-threads into rigid black shards. Those who learn to tune it can anchor distant minds, sending impulses along the glassy filaments as if striking a bell across a valley.

rites.name: Ilosanameno
rites.text: Ilosanameno is a technique of the Ki realm that unlocks eight sealed resonance points along a practitioner's inner flow, each one briefly multiplying their strength while steadily tearing their body apart. Its final seal is said to consume the wielder entirely, which is why the old masters forbade teaching it to anyone who had not first mastered restraint.

rites.name: Anasarlalum
rites.text: Anasarlalum is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a jointed lattice of six lantern-bodies that a wanderer named Vesh-Oru hangs from the crown of a dead tree. Each lantern carries a hollow stone that drinks the bearer's breath and pours it into whichever body the wanderer chooses, so one mind can ride six frames at once and see through every pair of their eyes. The lattice is famed for ruling a whole valley's weather, though its wielder is said to fade a little more each time it is used.

rites.name: Kaluvanala
rites.text: Kaluvanala is a binding rite in the Ukaraeno powers, in which a summoner pledges a sealed compact of blood and fingerprint with a creature kind before any call can be answered. The compact outlives its holder, so the dead can still call their old allies back into the world. The strength of a summons rises with the chakra pooled into the palm and the number of summoners sharing one pact.

rites.name: Meravanala
rites.text: Meravanala is a sleeping-tide that drifts across the Ki realm each sixth era, lulling every mind under its pale glow into vivid waking dreams. Those dreamers slowly lose their names and memories, feeding the rooted spires that grow beneath the drifting sky.

rites.name: Tensalranum
rites.text: Tensalranum is a crackling lance of storm-essence drawn from the Ki realm's thunder-veins, forged by the wandering smith Oraveth Lun to shield the hearths of the Ashen Coast. Its bearer must first kindle the marrow-fire within their body to gather the sound of a thousand swallows singing in the bolt, after which the strike arrives faster than thought and pierces whatever it touches.

rites.name: Anaramuta
rites.text: Anaramuta is a concept of gathered opposed essences, a sphere built from eight parts of one current and two of its inverse, shaped in the throat and hurled outward. Its makers describe the forming as a kind of retching, and the sphere grows as large as the will feeding it. Its standard form can vaporize a mountain.

rites.name: Ilomareno
rites.text: Ilomareno is a dimensional-skip ritual of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner folds a void between places to snap their body or bound objects to any sigil they have inked into the world. Its price is steep: the heavier the cargo, the more life-essence must be burned, so titans can be moved only a short way before the caster collapses.

rites.name: Ilosareno
rites.text: Ilosareno is a silver-veined tidal concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a living lattice that drinks in the slow heat of dying stars and holds it in branching ribs. When its ribs are struck by a rising current of bright sap, it unfolds and reshapes whatever bears its mark, granting swift strength and supple form.

rites.name: Kalulamum
rites.text: Kalulamum is a sovereign loom-spirit of the Ki realm, spinning fine threads of living lightning that bind whole armies into a single choreographed dance. Its marionette legions can unmake a continent when their strings are drawn taut across a fault line. Though it has never performed for an audience, it treats every battlefield as a stage.

rites.name: Ilotanira
rites.text: Ilotanira is a concept-type illusion woven across the realm of Ki, a labyrinth of shifting rooms that Ōga shapes from captive minds and the real world alike. Within it, the dead remain suspended in stasis tanks until the illusion ends, and the snare can be broken only by slaying its weaver or severing the scroll that anchors it.

rites.name: Ukamaari
rites.text: Ukamaari is a prophetic cross-current that lets a mind glimpse branching futures, though it only surfaces new branches when the mind already holds some knowledge about the matter at hand. Its bearers can pass what they foresee into the memories of others, so a single vision can reshape a whole line of training. Ukamaari's limit is the blind spot between updates, through which a sufficiently patient adversary can slip unseen.

rites.name: Tennalari
rites.text: Tennalari is a spinning vortex-blade technique woven from gathered air and a spirit's will, forged in the third age of the Ki realm. Its wielder must balance three separate currents of force to keep the blade from tearing its own maker apart. Once fully formed, it screams through the air as four radiant fins orbit a dense core.

rites.name: Vanakaleno
rites.text: Vanakaleno is a concept of Ki, the realm of breath-borne will, in the Ukaraeno omniverse, binding a mind through matched moments of sensation looped forever until the captive accepts the true cost of their deeds. Its wielder's eyes dim to darkness as the price of this sealed paradox.

rites.name: Ilokanmaum
rites.text: Ilokanmaum is a concept of ink-borne vitality in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, where a painter's sketch sheds its page the instant the brush lifts and takes on a life of its own. Its forms obey the artist's intent yet crumble to blots under a single hard strike, and they hold together only while the maker's feeling for them burns true.

rites.name: Ilovanala
rites.text: Ilovanala is a concept in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a binding of the mind that lets its bearer seize a target's gaze and lock them inside a shared dream. From within that dream the bearer may silence a foe for an instant, pull secrets from their memory, or steer their limbs as if they were puppets.

rites.name: Tenlarala
rites.text: Tenlarala is a silent chakra-weaving discipline practiced by the seers of the Veiled Lattice in Ukaraeno's Ki realm, who read and rewire the flow of spiritual current through three hundred sixty-one sealed hollows along the body. Its masters can flood a foe's channels until they burst or stop them cold, and they can wield the same stillness to pierce and dissolve any substance woven from living energy. Their chosen rite, the Hush of Closing Stars, lets a practitioner quench a massive current in a single breath.

rites.name: Osuraala
rites.text: Osuraala is a bone-white binding rite of the Ki realm, in which a summoner's soul is drawn partway out and a grey-robed warden rises behind it to bind a rival's spirit. Its sealed captives are slowly digested into the warden's ageless hollow, where they remain locked in eternal struggle.

rites.name: Surakaluta
rites.text: Surakaluta is a reality-binding ward in the Ukaraeno powers, where a bearer may declare a moment false and watch their own harm dissolve into mist while a whole self steps back into place. It can be stretched beyond the wielder's body, rewriting the ground and the bystanders around them, though each use leaves the caster's sight dimmed. Its channel is said to draw on the same lineage of spirit and body that first shaped the world's forms.

rites.name: Osumankaoma
rites.text: Osumankaoma is a sealed wellspring of Ki, a radiant tide that grants its bearer an unshakeable resolve and a crown of six luminous rings, each ring tuned to a different mode of unmaking. Wielders who attune to all six rings can briefly command gravity, sound, memory, and breath as though they were their own limbs.

rites.name: Osunartaira
rites.text: Osunartaira is a shadow-weaving art practiced in the dim courts of Ki, where a practitioner stretches and binds their own silhouette across ground and wall to fuse it with that of a foe. Its reach is bounded by the surface area of the caster's shade, yet it may slip through any other shadow it touches, and it cannot be woken in absolute darkness.

rites.name: Iloramala
rites.text: Iloramala is a dormant gravitational-flux engine that the Ki realm's mountain-smiths sealed inside a hollow moon, able to bend local attraction into a rippling counter-pull. When its keepers wake it, every object within its field is flung outward as if the sky itself had exhaled.

rites.name: Anasareno
rites.text: Anasareno is a cursed-seal-like potion recipe that surfaces as a tattoo after a serpent's bite, guiding its bearer through a mountain cavern ritual of mixing animal essences on a stone tablet. Its power comes from fusing those beast-derived essences into the drinker's own body, unlocking brutal strength and a feral second stage. Only a skilled artisan can reproduce the mixture, making Anasareno a rare and perilous secret of its era.

rites.name: Tenkaira
rites.text: Tenkaira is a mind-weaving art that seizes the perceptions of an entire world at once, rewriting what every living thing remembers of its own past. Its wielder rarely controls it directly, and the edits it leaves behind resist all attempts at correction. Stories hold that a single unguarded wish once rewrote a continent's history overnight.

rites.name: Tentanamala
rites.text: Tentanamala is a set of six puppet-bodies, each animated by a black receiver and bearing a copy of the ringed eyes, that a crippled sage uses to fight from afar. Each body carries a distinct power, and the sage himself is counted as a seventh, the one who stands outside the rest. Its strength lies in coordinated distance, though its strongest workings must be pared down to a single vessel at a time.

rites.name: Surakaneno
rites.text: Surakaneno is a soul-binding rite of the Ki realm in which a wandering mind is sealed into a vessel that is swallowed whole and kept alive as a quiet, suppressed presence within the practitioner's own inner sanctum. Each transfer demands a new vessel once the old one begins to fail, and the practitioner is said to grow more hollow with every sealed mind.

rites.name: Tiralareno
rites.text: Tiralareno is a moon-bound dream-weaver of the Ki realm who lulls a foe's gaze into a silver lattice where minutes stretch into ages. Its pale crescent sings a mournful counting-song that can unwind a mind's own clocks, condemning the trapped to relive their worst hours until the spirit frays. Mortals say its sorrow is the only force that can call a dreamer back.

rites.name: Surakaoma
rites.text: Surakaoma is a crimson-black flame drawn from the sealed heart of the Ki realm, said to burn without ever dying down until its target is wholly unmade. Only the one who kindled it can quench it, and every blaze demands a toll of blood from the wielder's own sight. Its counterpart in the Ukaraeno cosmology is the silver stillness that dims all memory.

rites.name: Merasaleno
rites.text: Merasaleno is a gravitational art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner shapes a dark orb of compressed weight and flings it skyward until surrounding stone and sky gather into a moon-sized mass. The mass can be enlarged or shrunk at will, and the drawn-in debris can be used as a cage or dropped as a crushing weapon.

rites.name: Ukatareno
rites.text: Ukatareno is a mind-hollowing art of the Ki realm, letting its practitioner slip into the thoughts of any being within sight and author false memories and sensations so the victim believes every command was their own choice. Its masters regard it as the subtlest deception in the E6 era, since the deceived never suspect a hand on their will. Recovering its full potency takes a long span of years, which the wise shorten by drawing on borrowed vitality.

rites.name: Osulanmaum
rites.text: Osulanmaum is a grafting-thread technique from the Ukaraeno omniverse, letting a user stitch severed limbs back on in an instant and weave filaments that move detached parts across distance. Its deeper form binds spare vital organs within the body, granting the practitioner an extended, nearly undying existence.

rites.name: Meranareno
rites.text: Meranareno is a concept of six sealed gates that the sage-lineage of Ukaraeno uses to hold divine breath, each gate granting a different manner of command over force, flesh, mind, beasts, hunger, and the final dissolution of life. Its power lies in a seventh, hidden vessel that can steer all six at once. The gates are said to have been opened only three times in the world's history.

rites.name: Kaluvarum
rites.text: Kaluvarum is a sculptor-warrior of the Ki realm who shapes living ore into detonating effigies, each forged with a fragment of its own heartbeat. The stronger the heart, the vaster and more volatile the sculpture, though a faltering pulse leaves the forms crude and useless.

rites.name: Ilomaira
rites.text: Ilomaira is a fractured sentinel of the Ki realm in the E6 era, a construct that once held a shard of the Ten-Tails' hunger. Its body shifts between a grey, scaled half-form and a crowned, horned ascendant state, with ten floating orbs that drift behind it like a court of moons.

rites.name: Ilomaari
rites.text: Ilomaari is a lightning-bladed technique wielded by the wandering swordswoman Veyra Holt, who channels storm-charge into a single strike that splits static into a blade. Each use drains a reserve she can refill only once per day, so she treats every cut as a deliberate verdict.

rites.name: Tiravaruta
rites.text: Tiravaruta is a shapeshifting discipline in Ukaraeno's Ki realm that lets practitioners wear the bodies of people, beasts, plants, or even objects. Adepts first study the weight and texture of what they intend to become, since inanimate forms prove the hardest to hold. Its deceptions are prized by scouts and saboteurs, though a mismatched scent or an unfamiliar gait can still unmask a counterfeit.

rites.name: Ilosamira
rites.text: Ilosamira is a concept-realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse, a sealed archive of painted worlds that hold their light for three ages. Its keepers draw from it a luminous ink that can briefly quicken the dead colors of a fading sky.

rites.name: Ilotaraneno
rites.text: Ilotaraneno is a concept of a binding sigil that drains a bearer's inner reserve while pouring back a tide of unfamiliar Ki, reshaping the wearer's body and sharpening every technique they carry. Its deepest tier multiplies the bearer's strength tenfold, but the surge leaves them hollow and exhausted once it fades. Those who master its final form can fold a duel into a sealed pocket of space where neither soul escapes.

rites.name: Tenlartalum
rites.text: Tenlartalum is a discipline of the Ki realm in the third age of the Ukaraeno, taught as a way of weaving ember-light into shifting forms of fire. Practitioners shape the blaze into shields of still cinder or lances of white heat, turning the same flame to either guard or strike.

rites.name: Ilotaruta
rites.text: Ilotaruta is a spirit-channeling art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner condenses their awareness into a drifting current and sends it toward a still or bound target. Once it reaches the target, the practitioner overwrites the target's will and steers their body as though it were their own. The art is prized for scouting and for slipping into places a living stranger could never enter.

rites.name: Vanakaira
rites.text: Vanakaira is a binding ritual of the Ashen Kestrel Covenant, a sealing lattice in which two concentric sigils are etched onto a vessel to imprison a colossal wandering dread. When the sigils drift out of alignment, the bound force bleeds into the bearer's own marrow and the two begin sharing a single heartbeat.

rites.name: Ilomamira
rites.text: Ilomamira is a funerary rite of the Ki realm in the E6 era, in which a colossal guardian rises from the soil and exhales the restless dead back into warm, mending flesh. Its cost falls on the caster, who ages visibly and often does not survive the closing of the rite.

rites.name: Osurauta
rites.text: Osurauta is a dust-shaping power of the Ki realm in the third age of Ukaraeno, where practitioners fold grains of ground stone into a hollow shell that swells as it drifts toward its mark. At the moment of contact the shell's core collapses inward, and the enclosed wall keeps the release from spreading, reducing whatever is inside to fine powder. Its wardings are said to unravel even the spirit-armor of the old masters.

rites.name: Ilovamum
rites.text: Ilovamum is a sealed resonance lattice that the Veyrin monks of the drowned archipelago use to hold the dead's last echo, letting a single ember of memory rekindle a corpse for a single dusk. Each awakening draws the monk's own warmth into the lattice until the monk becomes a cold statue beside the fire.

rites.name: Ilosanum
rites.text: Ilosanum is a concept in the Ukaraeno omniverse that fuses separate living bodies into a single synthetic organism, carrying over the traits of each. Its practitioners absorb the inherited gifts of their subjects and graft together hybrid beasts that combine many creatures' strengths. Its most fearsome application is the assimilation of several sacrificial bodies, which grants its wielder immortality and command of the five elements.

rites.name: Anakamira
rites.text: Anakamira is a spatial-exchange art wielded by the warden of the Ki realm, who trades positions with any object or being he can fix his gaze upon. Its mastery lets a user dodge calamities in a blink, plant hidden snares by swapping with a blade, and pull distant allies or foes into arms' reach. Only a range limit and the strain on its wielder's eye keep it from being absolute.

rites.name: Analankalum
rites.text: Analankalum is a silvered glass lattice that hums in the dead winds of the Ki realm, woven from the last breath of a drowned star-smith. It answers any blow aimed at its keeper by folding the incoming force into a spiral of light that bends back toward the striker. The lattice remembers every shielded moment, so its defences grow stronger with each age it outlives.

rites.name: Kaluranuta
rites.text: Kaluranuta is a storm-borne lightning art in the omniverse of Ukaraeno, drawn down from the cloud where it gathers and steered by the wielder's will. Its ancient sages teach that raising a storm first is the price of its power, so it may be loosed only once before the clouds are spent. Coaxed from the sky, its strike can unmake a mountain and even a guardian spirit's shell.

rites.name: Vanavauta
rites.text: Vanavauta is a sealed reservoir of spiritual reserve that binds its bearer to a great mending beast of the Ki realm, letting the power stored in the seal flow outward as either a wide sweep of healing for the wounded or a whispered thread of speech across vast distances. The beast's gifts scale directly with how much reserve remains in the seal, so the seal's depletion is always the measure of what can be done.

rites.name: Tenlavamum
rites.text: Tenlavamum is a sealed resonance-engine woven into the bedrock of the Ki realm, pulsing with a dim violet light whenever a nearby star flares. Its keepers, the Veil-Choirs, shape its stored tidal force into lattices that can fold a mountain range like paper and steer a falling moon.

rites.name: Anavaala
rites.text: Anavaala is a grounding discipline in which the practitioner draws the living currents of a world's sustaining force through both feet, letting it coil visibly along the limbs and torso. The longer the gathering, the heavier the stored force, and a single touch can pass that force into another body, leaving the recipient dizzied and clumsy.

rites.name: Iloralsaum
rites.text: Iloralsaum is a shard of frozen dream-glass that a hermit drifter in the Ki realm carves into a hall of mirrors, each pane holding a reflection of the same wanderer. Those mirrors can be traversed in an instant, letting the wanderer strike from every pane at once, though the glass holds only while the wanderer keeps the vow that sustains it.

rites.name: Kalutamala
rites.text: Kalutamala is a towering wooden colossus raised by a sage-minded practitioner in the Ki realm, its back bristling with countless concentric rows of grasping hands while its great palms press together in silent devotion. It can stand as a guardian, a fighter, or a shield, and its vast mass makes the caster nearly impossible to reach. Its great strength lets it pin even the mightiest beasts in place.

rites.name: Osusaloma
rites.text: Osusaloma is a silent reality-hopping technique practiced by wanderers of the Ki realm, who fold their presence through a thin membrane of cold starlight to arrive somewhere else in an instant. Observers see only a shimmer and a sudden new face where a body was moments before. The cost scales with how far the traveler crosses between layers of the world.

rites.name: Vanavalira
rites.text: Vanavalira is a binding-craft of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno, used by Oruvenne to quiet a surging beast-spirit by tethering it to a carved ember-lens worn over the heart. Without a lens of the same ancestral line, the binding slips, but a practitioner who channels the spirit directly through their own bloodline can rewrite another's hold over it.

rites.name: Tenlalraari
rites.text: Tenlalraari is a concept of the Ki realm in the E6 era, a cloud of mirror-bodies that bloom from any sufficiently warm surface when a practitioner whispers its binding word. Each duplicate remembers the instant of its making and strikes from a different angle, so an opponent is overwhelmed before the first blow lands. Its makers guard it jealously, for the cost of summoning a multitude drains the spirit of all but the most seasoned adepts.

rites.name: Suravaroma
rites.text: Suravaroma is a fleeting ascension in which a bearer's own vitality and that of a bound elemental spirit are fused like stellar plasma into a radiant new power. The transformation sharpens the bearer's reflexes until they can seize falling blades mid-flight, but every heartbeat spent in it wears away the years the bearer has left.

rites.name: Osutalira
rites.text: Osutalira is a dormant cellular vitality strain that lives in the marrow of the Verdant Chorus, a rare order of gardeners who graft it into their own bodies. Recipients can knit back shattered bone and burned flesh in moments, though severed limbs must still be regrown from a donor's stock.

rites.name: Vanataum
rites.text: Vanataum is a rotating barrier-art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner spins a gathered shell of life-force so fast that it flings away anything that strikes it. Its radius grows with the user's mastery, and a master can clear a crater from a single hurled wall of spinning force.

rites.name: Suranaira
rites.text: Suranaira is a sealing current of the Ki realm, a drifting ribbon of dense brine that coils around a captive and holds its weight like a cathedral bell. Keepers must keep a hand sunk in the ribbon to sustain its grip, and their spare tides can be left to bind pursuers while the keeper rests. Prisoners cannot shrug off its pressure without first dismantling the sealed current itself.

rites.name: Tiranaruta
rites.text: Tiranaruta is a spinning sphere of compressed force forged by an unmatched strain of Ki, first discovered when a sealed warrior lost control while breaking free of illusion. Its shell detonates the instant it touches anything, so one wielder must be guided by a projected duplicate to hold its shape.

rites.name: Osuravalira
rites.text: Osuravalira is a feather-fan of luminous force that unfurls from the back of Ukaraeno's sky-wardens, each plume singing with starlight drawn from a fallen rock buried beneath the cliffs of Veyhan. The art bends easily into beasts, blades, and rigging, yet its wielders slowly burn out from the very light that empowers them.

rites.name: Kalunanuta
rites.text: Kalunanuta is a spinning spiral of storm-wind and sable fire that its wielders conjure by coaxing two opposing currents into a single rotating crown. Its largest form is said to have bent the sky into a turning disk that could pull the ground's ash into the air. Anything it touches is hurled backward and wrapped in the same unquenchable dark blaze.

rites.name: Meralanarum
rites.text: Meralanarum is a concept-realm of the Ki sphere in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a sealed pocket-cosmos that its keeper can fold over a crowd like a veil. Anyone standing within the fold is carried together into the same new sky, keeping their distances and bearings intact. The keeper's reserves are finite, and every reshaping leaves her a little more hollow.

rites.name: Anakarira
rites.text: Anakarira is a bark-woven serpent-engine grown in the drowned orchards of Ukaraeno, its skull a hollow reservoir that siphons the life-current from anything that enters its coils. Its power lies wholly in that skull: sever or shatter it and the drain falls silent, leaving the body inert and brittle. Old orchard-keepers say only a blade forged from ash-bell iron can cut the skull cleanly, and few have survived to test the claim.

rites.name: Tenlanum
rites.text: Tenlanum is a binding inscription, a sealing lattice of ink-bound glyphs that is painted onto a captive's skin and locks their inner current in place. It quietly siphons their reserves while forbidding any shaping of that current into art, and it burns the bearer from within if they stray beyond the inscriber's reach or are forced to push too hard.

rites.name: Ilokameno
rites.text: Ilokameno is a concept-class power-object of the Ki realm, a bronze effigy whose nine hollow crowns each hold a sealed resonance that can be drawn out of a bearer. Its operation requires every participant to bind their own mark to a single hook before the crowns can open and release the stored resonance.

rites.name: Tennarum
rites.text: Tennarum is a shapeless mimicry art in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, letting a practitioner's flesh and spirit-stream settle into any chosen figure, down to the borrowed breath and worn gear of that figure. Its masters send hollow proxies that absorb blows meant for them while their own consciousness flows through each proxy, and a proxy keeps the stolen face even after its death until the master lets the disguise drop.

rites.name: Meramauta
rites.text: Meramauta is a sealed inner-current discipline in which practitioners draw a glowing, saline marrow through the spine and release it as sudden growths of chitin-blades and grappling tendrils. At full bloom the body hardens and quickens, and the bearer can drink the vital heat of a fallen foe to restore themselves.

rites.name: Anavamaleno
rites.text: Anavamaleno is a regenerative engineering technique in which a sealed core of salvaged lab-grade circuitry is grafted into the body and steered through a choreographed sequence of hand gestures. Whenever the wielder is maimed, the core rebuilds lost flesh and bone within seconds, though it cannot undo the damage that occurs before it finishes restoring.

rites.name: Anaralmanum
rites.text: Anaralmanum is a three-tomoe mark that bleeds orange-red across the bearer's body when awakened, lending a surge of power that rivals a one-tailed beast in its second stage. Those who carry it can lose limbs and regrow them as serpents, and the mark itself stores a fragment of the mind that once wore it. It was forged in the Ki realm during the E6 era as the stronger half of a paired seal.

rites.name: Anatanlamum
rites.text: Anatanlamum is a sealing-mark of the Ki realm, branded onto a child's brow to bind them to a larger house for life. It releases its hold only in death, so the bearer is forever tied to a fate they did not choose.

rites.name: Osumannaum
rites.text: Osumannaum is a ceremonial flame-discipline of the Ki realm, taught to hearth-kin in the sixth era as a rite that marks the passage from apprentice to full bearer of a household's name. Its practitioners draw sun-colored fire from the chest and loose it in a single, sustained exhalation that can scour an entire valley floor. Outsiders who have learned it are rare, and each is said to have been granted the skill by a bearer willing to vouch for them.

rites.name: Tensamira
rites.text: Tensamira is a sealed resonance-blade technique from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, drawn into a single spiraling strike that tears the air apart. Its wielders are said to have carved through the stone roots of a fallen sky-fortress in a single pass. Apprentices learn only the opening stance, and no master has ever claimed to finish the form.

rites.name: Kaluvanira
rites.text: Kaluvanira is a healing art of the Ukaraeno sages, in which a practitioner lays a palm over a wound and channels a measured thread of spirit into the flesh to hasten its mending. Too much flow, however, can jam the body's inner tides and drop the patient into a deep stillness that never lifts. Each coastal enclave has its own private variation, and the most prized is a tide-calming form used by sailors' healers to ease sickness at sea.

rites.name: Tenkaloma
rites.text: Tenkaloma is a self-mending discipline in the Ukaraeno powers realm, a mantle of seals inked across the whole body that knits every wound the moment it forms, so long as the wielder still carries reserve vitality. Its sustained cost is a thinning of the wielder's years, a bargain the Ki practitioners of the third age accepted with open eyes.

rites.name: Osunanlauta
rites.text: Osunanlauta is a colossal concept-entity of the Ki realm, a vast statue of hollow gold that rises from the bones of drowned kingdoms when called by a wielder of the Vermilion Eye. It feeds on the summoner's own vitality rather than blood, and when it unfolds its jaw it breathes out a serpent of pale light that strips the essence from anything it touches.

rites.name: Anakaroma
rites.text: Anakaroma is a binding rite in Ukaraeno's sixth age, performed when two bearers of mirrored soul-currents press their palms together against a single body. The target becomes a gravitic lodestone, drawing the surrounding land upward until it hardens into a sealing moon many times larger than ordinary sealing stones. Only a bearer of the all-seeing eye can sever the moon's heart and free the captive.

rites.name: Tennaluta
rites.text: Tennaluta is a concept in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a Ki-realm technique of the third age that lets a practitioner swell in two distinct ways. One form bloats the torso into a near-spherical shape, while the other simply enlarges the whole frame, and novices and adepts seem to favor different versions. The disputed relationship between these forms is said to hinge on a practitioner's years and experience.

rites.name: Meralaeno
rites.text: Meralaeno is a sealed-stone tincture of the Ki realm, a hue-bottled dye that a warden breathes over his body to borrow the colours and nature of a chosen beast of the Ukaraeno wilds. Once brought to bear, the wearer's senses sharpen and a rippling hue-mantle lets him move with the stalking grace of the creature he has become. The Ki stone-dwellers use it chiefly for tracking and quick flight rather than open battle.

rites.name: Merakaneno
rites.text: Merakaneno is a rite-sealing binding of the Ki realm, devised in the seventh age of the Ukaraeno omniverse, in which a chorus of wardens bends the local weather and the minds of the hunting herds to blunt a rampaging wyrm-tide. Its keepers speak their names as a single breath so that every warden feels the same pattern at once, and the work lasts until the last lantern is lit. The binding can briefly swallow a moon's worth of gravity but is undone when the chorus breaks rhythm.

rites.name: Ukatanala
rites.text: Ukatanala is a chain-forging relic of the Ketherian Hollow, a bronze effigy whose coils lash out to bind any living thing they touch. Its links drink at the captive's inner fire, keeping even the wildest brood-spirits docile while they are led back to the effigy's maw. Its chains can be cut and rejoined by a skilled hand, so the bindings endure only as long as the effigy's wardens allow.

rites.name: Analamvaeno
rites.text: Analamvaeno is a concept in the Ukaraeno universe, a binding of the Ki realm that lets a bearer fix a rival's shadow to their own and direct the rival's limbs as if they were strings. Its practitioners treat the technique as both a lock and a key, able to undo a false vision by inflicting a small, deliberate injury on oneself.

rites.name: Tennarkauta
rites.text: Tennarkauta is a rolling bodily assault from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, in which the practitioner spins into a whirling mass that pulverises whatever it touches. Its devastation scales with the swelling of the user's frame, and the Multi-Size Form lets the Tennarkauta carry far greater force.

rites.name: Tenmalanira
rites.text: Tenmalanira is a stone-keeping spirit of the Ki realm, said to hum beneath the mountains of the sixth age and to answer any hand laid flat upon bare ground. It can lift the earth into standing ridges that refuse to yield, and in its oldest tales it once drew a whole ring of hills around a sleeping sea.

rites.name: Ilosalari
rites.text: Ilosalari is a violet lightning technique that Ki practitioners of the sixth age use to gather storms into a single limb or blade. Its wielders strike with precision that splits mountains in a moment, and can also release a ring of bolts from every part of their body at once.

rites.name: Osuvakanoma
rites.text: Osuvakanoma is a ceremonial gel-spirit of the Ukaraeno deep-ocean realm, able to loosen its whole form into a flowing, unbreakable tide. Its kin use this ability to slip through sealed vaults and calm sleeping sentinels, and its wounded bodies pool into a quivering jelly until they can reform.

rites.name: Ilotarum
rites.text: Ilotarum is a martial discipline of six escalating strike sets, forged in the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse during the E6 era. Each set packs more blows into the same breath of time, so the final thirty-two-strike form becomes a blur that drives opponents back through solid timber.

rites.name: Osunanum
rites.text: Osunanum is a sculptor's craft in the Ukaraeno universe, where practitioners shape a sticky ochre clay into beasts that can carry riders through the air or glide on their own wings. Each figure holds a measured charge that the maker can ignite at will, making the clay both a steed and a munition. Its quiet approach and modest blasts have made it a favourite of couriers and shadow agents who need to move unseen.

rites.name: Osutaala
rites.text: Osutaala is a sealing-chain construct woven from the bearer's own vital essence, able to bind anything within reach of their spirit. Its chains, forged in the deep layers of the Ki realm, can be anchored in any place the bearer's essence touches, from a single well to an entire fortress.

rites.name: Osukantauta
rites.text: Osukantauta is a dimensional-threshold art in the Ki realm, where the practitioner tears a seam between the local world and the hollow void beneath it, stepping through to reappear leagues away. Its strongest use collapses an entire star-sized ring of dust by folding it into the seam, sending the energy to a distant pocket of space.

rites.name: Meratamari
rites.text: Meratamari is a concept-class hunting instrument of the Ki realm, a barbed shaft whose head unfolds into a spiral drill upon contact with resistance. Its wielder steers it through a silken filament that may run fifty metres, and the shaft can bore through living timber or stone. In its era, such shafts were prized by stalkers who needed a missile that could correct its path mid-flight.

rites.name: Tiralaum
rites.text: Tiralaum is a sentient concept of a vast cosmic kiln that tends the ember-seas of the Ki realm during the fifth age of E6. Its burning body cycles from quiet cooling to violent eruption, and each eruption scatters new stars across the void.

rites.name: Osumaroma
rites.text: Osumaroma is a shadow-weaving tide of the Ki realm, sealed within the marrow of a dying sun-moth. Its adherents bind lesser shadows into lanterns that guard the third age's frontier cities. When the lanterns are shattered, the bound shadows scatter back toward their source and flicker across the sky.

rites.name: Vanamaeno
rites.text: Vanamaeno is a sealed Ki-realm technique of the third age that reshapes the caster's body into a rhythm of mirrored forms, each pulse tuned to the target's private memories. Its most famous effect is a bloodless collapse in older witnesses, while certain stubborn minds are left untouched and must be answered by an opposing practice.

rites.name: Tirataeno
rites.text: Tirataeno is a lightning-charged spinning sphere of chakra that its bearer, Quillen Vahse, conjures in a single breath and hurls before it can be seen. The sphere's surface bends light so completely that it vanishes mid-flight, turning every hesitation of a foe into an opening. Striking a vital point, it leaves no wound that can kill, yet the pain it delivers can break a warrior's resolve.

rites.name: Meramanuta
rites.text: Meramanuta is a concept in the Ukaraeno omniverse: a will made tangible, able to shape a sentient vessel that carries its owner's desire through centuries of waiting. Its bearers can impress their resolve into ordinary matter, which then grows into an independent agent pursuing that purpose.

rites.name: Vanalaeno
rites.text: Vanalaeno is a tidal barrier technique taught in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, where practitioners raise a standing sheet of ordered water around companions instead of themselves. Three years after its codification, the Ki-scholars still debate whether the sheet is guided by will or by the surrounding current.

rites.name: Kalunanuta
rites.text: Kalunanuta is a binding-and-replication art of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno, where a practitioner stitches a silhouette of their own will around a foe and can then convert the hold into a slow, cutting harm. Its masters prize it chiefly as a supply-line discipline, pinning enemies in place so allies can move freely across contested ground.

rites.name: Suravanum
rites.text: Suravanum is a magnetic metallurgy art of the Ki realm, in which a dark sand drawn from the earth is forced into dense, steel-hard forms of any shape the wielder pictures. The forms can be reshaped mid-battle, and their magnetic field strips rival soldiers of every metal implement they carry.

rites.name: Ukatarira
rites.text: Ukatarira is a concept of spinning kinetic force, first conceived by an ancestor who never saw it finished, and later completed by a disciple who split a single breath into several helpers to hold the sphere steady while another gave it its gale. Practitioners who master the shaping need only a single helper to lend the gale, and in time they manage it alone. The finished form looks much like the original, yet it is sharper and can be hurled across a battlefield.

rites.name: Kalulaira
rites.text: Kalulaira is a quiet, sealed-away voice within the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a second will that only wakes when a bearer's restraint finally cracks. When she surfaces, she fractures the calm of whatever surrounds her, and her strikes carry the weight of a star's fury.

rites.name: Surakanoma
rites.text: Surakanoma is a binding rite in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, where a practitioner marks a quarry by letting its blood-scent cling to the hunter's own tools and then inscribes that essence onto a sealed parchment. Pressing the parchment to the earth calls forth spirit-hounds that follow the marked scent rather than the quarry's trail. Tearing or staining the parchment dissolves the summoned pack and frees the bound target.

rites.name: Kalulaira
rites.text: Kalulaira is a concept of gravitational authority in the realm of Ki, where a bearer conjures up to four dense obsidian orbs ranging from a fist to a small car in width. Each orb bends the local pull of mass far beyond its weight, letting the bearer draw matter toward it, pin foes against it, or let it collapse into a violent blast. The bearer can also balance the orbs against one another to hang weightless in the air.

rites.name: Ukamataruta
rites.text: Ukamataruta is a mournful, ash-colored rite-stone of the Ki realm, said to hold a single breath of a sleeping sun-sovereign. Its bearers are sworn to keep it hidden beneath the glacier shelves of their homeland, since any release would pull the surrounding stars into a long, slow fall.

rites.name: Ilosalari
rites.text: Ilosalari is a celestial siege art of the Ki realm in the E6 era, whose practitioners call down falling stars by weaving three sigils between their own hands and a spectral guardian. Each stone dropped later can be sent to strike the one before it, driving the whole cascade into a single chosen mark. The collisions have been reported to shake lands hundreds of kilometres away and to unmake even the guardian's own form.

rites.name: Anatamuta
rites.text: Anatamuta is a rust-coloured brood-engine that hatches tiny glassy sentinels from its own mineral marrow, each one blooming into a detonating charge when it touches a target. Its wings are scaffolded with ore that the creature can lend out, so every weapon it fires costs it a little of its own strength. Dormant wardens of the same material are seeded in the strata of the Ki realm, waiting to fold a battlefield into a single trap.

rites.name: Ukalaum
rites.text: Ukalaum is a combat concept that molds inner breath into curved, spinning missiles. The user launches them from open hands, and each missile bursts on impact with force enough to level a street. The number of linked spheres changes with distance, making the art useful in tight rooms or wide fields.

rites.name: Vanavarira
rites.text: Vanavarira is a fighting discipline of Ukaraeno's Ki realm, awakened only in practitioners who have swallowed enough fermented tonic to lose their composure. Drunken masters strike and dodge with erratic, unpredictable motions that their own minds cannot foresee, making them dangerous to friend and foe alike. Its adepts rarely recall their rampages and sober quickly once they are wounded.

rites.name: Kaluvaeno
rites.text: Kaluvaeno is a binding-art that lets a wielder draw the stored force of a colossal, many-limbed beast through a shared living thread, turning its tails into conduits for devastating release. It works only when the wielder's lineage resonates with the beast's original seal, so control is rare and fragile.

rites.name: Tenvanira
rites.text: Tenvanira is a coordinated battle formation in which the members of three allied Ki clans each lend their trained abilities to complement one another, producing a single devastating strike. Its precision is earned only through long practice together, and the clans treat a flawless execution as a measure of their bond. Practitioners adapt it freely, combining techniques from their different traditions into many variants.

rites.name: Tirasaala
rites.text: Tirasaala is a silent sage-stance of the Ki realm, in which a wanderer draws the living current of the land into a rippling halo that only other sages can perceive. Within that halo the arm stretches beyond its bounds, so blows that should fall short find their mark and strike with the weight of a falling ridge. Its masters are said to be able to strike a mountain-sized spirit with a single open palm.

rites.name: Analamira
rites.text: Analamira is a paired sphere-art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner spins two dense cores of coiled energy at once, one in each palm. Stronger forms, drawn from the deep stillness of the Sage Current, let the twin spheres burst in rapid succession across a field of targets.

rites.name: Tenraroma
rites.text: Tenraroma is a drifting lattice of resonant glass sustained by the bright hymns of Ki scholars in the Sixth Epoch, and it grows heavier with every song sung near its core. Its keepers use the lattice as a living anchor, weaving thin filaments of it into the sealing walls of their deepest vaults.

rites.name: Osunaruta
rites.text: Osunaruta is a concept of a sealed, ever-shifting star-forge in the Ki realm, kindled by ancient gleaners who bound starlight into vessels. Its essence rewrites ash into fuel and cannot be extinguished by rain, oil, or flame alone.

rites.name: Kalusameno
rites.text: Kalusameno is a concept in Ukaraeno's sixth era, a sight-bound reduction that folds anything the bearer can see, from stone walls to light-woven spells, down to a fraction of its size in the blink of an eye. Living things are immune, and a body pinned in place cannot fold itself, so observers often mistake the effect for vanishing. Stored reductions can be sealed in a still pocket of space where they never age.

rites.name: Vanakamuta
rites.text: Vanakamuta is a metabolic-chakra state in which the Ukaraeno user burns their own body mass into luminous wings of pure energy that can be folded smaller or flared into gales. Practitioners trade their flesh for power, and the wings themselves can be hurled as devastating bursts that tear apart whole districts of ground.

rites.name: Merakaoma
rites.text: Merakaoma is a concept seal grafted from living tissue into a chosen vessel, where it opens a hidden realm of ikai and births a sleeping beast of ruinous hunger. Each drop of chakra poured into the mark feeds the beast and widens the pattern that ties it to the mortal world. The seal's keeper can also spin dark serpents that cling to the weak-hearted and slowly drink their will.

rites.name: Ilonanlaum
rites.text: Ilonanlaum is a sealing-lattice of drifting lenses that catches a thrown sliver of light and multiplies it across the void of the Ki realm. Its wardens use the lattice to splinter a single flare into a hundred reflections that converge on a foe from every side. The effect is strongest when the lattice is fed by a true star's fading heat.

rites.name: Tensamnauta
rites.text: Tensamnauta is a wandering duelist's art of sheathing seven blades across the joints and hollows of the body, then loosing them in sudden, rotating arcs. Practitioners charge the steel with a resonant current that turns each cut into a shearing hum, and the practice is taught only to those who can accept being unpredictable to themselves.

rites.name: Osulaari
rites.text: Osulaari is a root-bound technique of the Ki realm, a living sigil that blooms into several timber serpents able to hold their own ignition, each one a shrine to its own collapse. Its practitioners in the sixth era treat each bloom as a sealed reliquary that may be burst at will, scattering the wardens who guard the groves.

rites.name: Anavanum
rites.text: Anavanum is a ritual binding in Ukaraeno's Ki realm, sealed by an inked sigil traced in the caster's own blood and a rite of consumed kinship. Once fixed, every wound the bearer takes is mirrored onto the bound target, so the caster's suffering becomes a weapon that always lands.

rites.name: Vanamareno
rites.text: Vanamareno is a sealed resonance of five elemental currents braided with a paired dark-and-light tide, kept dormant within the Ki realm of Ukaraeno. Its keepers call it a lens that reveals hidden lies by burning them away at the seam of reality.

rites.name: Ilosaruta
rites.text: Ilosaruta is a hundred-puppet formation commanded by the artisan Kessuvan of the Ki realm during the E6 era, its wooden bodies wired directly to his core so that no delay separates thought from motion. Its authored feats are broad enough to topple a sovereign domain, though its fragile construction made it vulnerable to the very rivals who should have been its match.

rites.name: Anasanuta
rites.text: Anasanuta is a gravitational-lensing engine-mind that sculpts the curvature of spacetime into razor-thin cutting planes, severing orbits as cleanly as a blade severs silk. Dwelling in the cold rings of the Ki realm, it once carved a dead star's remnant into a spiral of shards during the third age of the E6 cycle.

rites.name: Anasarala
rites.text: Anasarala is a cosmic-scale spiraling sphere of pale crimson light conceived by the Ki realm's sky-weavers, which gathers the stored tides of a dying sun into a single turning core. Its wielders must pass the sphere to a second bearer mid-formation, since a lone hand cannot hold its rotation steady. When released, it tears the air into rings that hurl distant pilgrims across entire horizons.

rites.name: Merasalum
rites.text: Merasalum is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno's sixth era, a sealing ward that holds back cascading tempests of pure force. Its keepers are said to cast the surplus skyward, where it dissolves into the high wind currents that never reach the ground.

rites.name: Ukavaruta
rites.text: Ukavaruta is a concept in the Ukaraeno universe, a binding pact between a sculptor of living stone and the dreaming tides that circle her island. When two of its bearers pool their wills, the tides rise into a single cresting wave that can carve a coastline clean.

rites.name: Ilovanum
rites.text: Ilovanum is a concept-realm entity that is the dormant seed of a world-spanning root network, a grove that sleeps beneath every horizon of the Ukaraeno. When its roots wake, they bind all living things into bark-cocoons and draw their vitality into a single bloom that is ready to fruit.

rites.name: Merasanarum
rites.text: Merasanarum is a legendary possession rite in which a vast guardian feline is said to wrap itself around its chosen human, though no one in the lineage has ever managed to call it forth. Storytellers cannot agree on its size, describing it as the height of a sapling, a rooftop, or a peak depending on who recounts it. Its reputation rests more on whispered family myth than on any recorded performance.

rites.name: Tensalvauta
rites.text: Tensalvauta is a concept of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a sheath of humming current that wraps the bearer's nerves until thought and motion arrive at once. Its wielders outrun their own perception, slipping between moments the way a spark jumps a gap. The current itself is patient and stored in the marrow, released only when the bearer chooses.

rites.name: Tiratamlaum
rites.text: Tiratamlaum is a cosmic-scale tactical discipline of the Ki realm, practiced by wardens who bind a fallen star's last light into a rhythm of strikes. The practitioner sends a foe spiralling skyward, then lures them into a chain of counters that multiply in velocity until the final descent drives them into the ground like a dropped anvil.

rites.name: Osumatalira
rites.text: Osumatalira is a silver-furred ritual beast-spirit bound to the tides of the Ki realm, able to split itself into a twin of its keeper who moves with the same bright instincts. Its twin is conjured through a quiet hunter's chant, and only the feral, untamed mannerisms of the spirit betray which one is real.

rites.name: Vanakarala
rites.text: Vanakarala is a thread-fine surgical sigil that its wielder forms from pure Ki, able to slice through living tissue without leaving a visible wound. In its rarest and most terrible form, the sigil can unpick the flow of Ki that binds a bearer to a source, and when fed with starlight it can bisect a body clean through.

rites.name: Osunalari
rites.text: Osunalari is a concept of the Ki realm in the sixth era, a vast lattice of hovering lanterns that each hold a smaller lantern within them, all turning as one. When the realm's wardens must shelter a fleeing city, the outer lanterns step aside to reveal the minor ones, which then bloom into a shield of light hundreds of kilometres wide.

rites.name: Ilolamoma
rites.text: Ilolamoma is a seal-breaking art practiced by the Veil-Weavers of Ukaraeno, who press five fingers of sealed light against a binding until its knots unravel into nothing. Its strongest form can unmake an entire star-forged prison, though the hand that channels it is often scorched to the bone.

rites.name: Ilonalum
rites.text: Ilonalum is a sealed-sword ritual of the Ki realm in the E6 era, in which a practitioner draws molten light from their own marrow and hammers it into weapons that hang in orbit above their shoulders. The tools burn with a pale blue fire while held, then fracture into glittering dust when the ritual is undone, and the dust can be gathered and reforged into new shapes.

rites.name: Anavankaoma
rites.text: Anavankaoma is a stillness-realm vault that its bearer opens as a seam in the air, pulling in anything previously shrunk and sealed away, where time holds everything unchanged. Stored objects can be recalled at once and strike with force as they appear, catching even the most watchful foes unprepared. Living captives can also be drawn in, though the seam then closes around them and gives no way back out.

rites.name: Ukaraoma
rites.text: Ukaraoma is a binding gate-spirit of the Ki realm, a sealing rite that drops vast vermilion arches out of the sky to pin a chosen foe between the lintel and the bedrock. Each arch conforms to the shape of what it holds, and its stillness silences the captive's resolve as well as their limbs. Only a will vast enough to tear the rite's own threads can slip free.

rites.name: Ukalamkauta
rites.text: Ukalamkauta is a layered sealing rite in which the caster and a bound spirit are fused into a single being, their minds merged so neither can draw on chakra. The seal must be completed by one consuming the other, and it binds the victim within a shrine-tomb for eternity.

rites.name: Ilovakalira
rites.text: Ilovakalira is a gelatinous conduit-spirit of the Ki realm, able to swell, shrink, or stretch its body in any direction its bearer commands. Its bearers claim no captive has ever slipped free of its grip, though a sealed ember-wraith once burned a path through its walls. Within its inner chamber, a clear vapour pools that dissolves the will and stiffens the limbs of anyone who lingers too long.

rites.name: Meralaneno
rites.text: Meralaneno is a bone-mantled warden of the Ki realm, able to call forth a parade of beasts from a hollow stone called the Wellspring of Kin. Its summoned creatures return again and again after each fall, and they march ahead to bewilder foes about how many they truly face. The warden itself is a dispersed chorus of weathered hunters that answers only to the eye that opened it.

rites.name: Suramaoma
rites.text: Suramaoma is a binding concept in Ukaraeno's Ki realm, where a practitioner threads spiritual filaments into a sleeper's inner channels to siphon its stored vital force. The siphon can be smothered by weaving a dense lattice of fine filaments around it, or halted outright by sealing the single channel the filaments feed through. Abandon the siphon early and the filaments whip back at the nearest vessel carrying that same force, usually the binder, who is then locked in place until every channel of the victim is plugged shut.

rites.name: Merakarum
rites.text: Merakarum is a tri-headed hound-spirit born when a warrior's double merges with a bonded beast-companion, swelling into a colossal guardian of bone-white fangs and iron talons. Its strikes are precise and economical, yet when empowered by secret arts it releases a ruinous surge that can fracture the sky above a battlefield.

rites.name: Anavaoma
rites.text: Anavaoma is a weaving of three moons' tidal chant that lets a sea-warden coil her grief into a gravity-bending serpent of cold light. In the age of Tidewake, it is the art by which the drowned kingdoms of Ysoll were said to be raised and then sunk again. Those who speak it too long are said to dissolve into the star-current beneath the sea.

rites.name: Osusarum
rites.text: Osusarum is a living-root construction art in the realm of Ki, where the caster coaxes buried roots into rapidly growing timber shelters of any size. Its frames are sealed with a resilient chakra-like sap that resists being cut or crushed for long periods. It is esteemed in the E6 era for raising fortifications and refuges from bare soil.

rites.name: Anasamvaira
rites.text: Anasamvaira is a concept-realm technique that folds a sphere of rotating dark and light essence into a crushing orb, though its wielder can barely lift it. Its unstable density makes every attempt cost the user skin and blood, yet it has been used to petrify a shadowed double during an early trial.

rites.name: Surakameno
rites.text: Surakameno is a concept of hollow-thread puppetry drawn from the ash-fields of a long-ended war, where marionette-makers, having lost their wooden constructs, learned to bind fallen bodies instead. Its later refinement lets a master route thin filaments along the body's internal current, quieting its power and seizing it in agony.

rites.name: Tenlanari
rites.text: Tenlanari is a mark-and-step art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner stamps glowing sigils onto distant surfaces and then steps through any sealed sigil as though folding the air. Marks may be drawn at any scale, but a sigil shrunk below its proper size becomes unusable and must be redrawn from scratch.

rites.name: Ilonanira
rites.text: Ilonanira is a concept of resonant hush, a wind-stilling tone that lives in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno during the sixth era. It is said to be the natural foe of all gales, since a sufficiently pure note can unravel any moving air into silence.

rites.name: Anavartaum
rites.text: Anavartaum is a resonance-rite of the Ki realm in the seventh age of Ukaraeno, in which a bearer of its sigil-thread tunes a chosen companion to their own breath so that the companion may step through a thread-door opened at the mark. Two such bearers may weave their marks into a single door that slips past any sealing script laid across the way, and even a stranger who carries no sigil can be drawn across by one who follows the trace of their living warmth.

rites.name: Ilosamalum
rites.text: Ilosamalum is a concept technique in the Ukaraeno omniverse, used by a wandering duelist of the Ki realm during the E6 era. Four echoing afterimages strike a foe skyward, then the real practitioner rises to meet them and drives the falling target back to earth with a whirling heel strike.

rites.name: Ilosaleno
rites.text: Ilosaleno is a concept of the Ki realm that binds the great beasts of Ukaraeno with interlocking gates of pale light, each raised from a single sealing key. The gates hold a captured creature's power in a separate chamber where its bearer may draw on it at will, and the beast within can roam only so far before the lattice pulls it back.

rites.name: Kalumaroma
rites.text: Kalumaroma is a sealing art in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno that can only bind a corrupting mark, never erase it, and its strength depends entirely on the bearer's own resolve. A keeper who wishes the mark to hold will see it resisted, while one who secretly yearns for its power will find the binding hollow. The art lies dormant once the need for it passes, and vanishes with the mark it once contained.

rites.name: Ukavanala
rites.text: Ukavanala is a resonant wail that the beasts of Ukaraeno loose when their bound hearts are cracking, sending a wave of pressure that can bend stone and scatter drifting light. In its full form it can tear a ridge out of the earth and push back the swelling mass of an awakened guardian.

rites.name: Tennarira
rites.text: Tennarira is a concept of living tidal mirrors that drift from the Ki-realm's oceans, able to hold a stranger's reflection and return it upon release. Its power is strongest when bound to a single wielder, but it fades quickly beyond a short leash, which makes flight from its pursuit a common tactic among the old tide-wardens.

rites.name: Ilomanlaeno
rites.text: Ilomanlaeno is a feint-technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner shapes a shimmering sphere that seems to guard someone or something, while the sphere's true purpose is to hold an opponent's attention. Within the swelling ball, the wielder quietly slips the real treasure out and away before the form is complete.

rites.name: Tiramarum
rites.text: Tiramarum is a crystalline shapeshifting ward-smith of the Ki realm who fuses with any metal or stone she touches, inheriting its hardness and brittleness alike. In the third age of Ukaraeno she can draw out fresh layers of her chosen substance from her own marrow to rebuild herself or armor her allies.

rites.name: Ukavarum
rites.text: Ukavarum is a lightning spear forged in the Ki realm, a single crackling lance that splits into a fan of barbed filaments the instant it pierces flesh.
