Its wielders can also let it spread into a humming blade, which serves as a sword when their weapon is lost. Taught in the era of the third age, it was used to cut open an ancient sealed guardian.

rites.name: Ilomaari
rites.text: Ilomaari is a gravitational discipline taught in the hollow spires of the Veil-thinned highlands, where practitioners pull and push mass through a lattice of tuned vacancy. Each drawn force must rest before it can be drawn again, and the wielder's breath slowly thins with every overextended pull. Its greatest rite, the Ember Wellspawn, collapses a dark cinder into a sphere that gathers surrounding rock into a moving hill-sized body.

rites.name: Surasaira
rites.text: Surasaira is a sword-forging discipline of the Ki realm, in which a wielder's life-force hardens into a blade that can reshape itself into broadswords, barbed staves, or crescent axes beyond the length of the steel it grows from. Its projectiles take the form of spinning discs and spears, shaped by whatever weapon the wielder had last formed.

rites.name: Ukasaloma
rites.text: Ukasaloma is a mind-swapping ward that binds a sparring partner's consciousness inside a waiting puppet, leaving the caster's own body open and exposed while the bond holds. Any harm dealt to the vessel echoes back onto the caster's true flesh unless they sever the ward in time.

rites.name: Anakalum
rites.text: Anakalum is a living-tissue technique in the world of Ukaraeno, where microscopic engineered filaments drift through the bloodstream and let the bearer reshape flesh into blades, plates, hooks, or hurled shards. When a limb is lost, the wielder can simply stretch their body's substance across the gap and form a working replacement.

rites.name: Osuratanari
rites.text: Osuratanari is a sealing sigil carved into the hollow bones of a drowned sky-whale, used by the tide-priests of Mirrowen to bind rampaging storms inside living vessels. Its binding is said to outlast the wrath of any tempest, though the sealed storm slowly gnaws at its keeper's memories.

rites.name: Anamarsaeno
rites.text: Anamarsaeno is a soul-sealing rite cast by a single practitioner, drawing trapped spirits out of their flesh and binding them within a barrier where they remain conscious but slowly fade. The bodies left behind hover at the edge of stillness, and only a precise touch of spiritual energy can coax a soul home again.

rites.name: Anasamira
rites.text: Anasamira is a concept in the Ukaraeno universe, a realm of the Ki that its builders treat as a living sea of resonant roots. Its signature act is to coil beneath a field and rise as a forest of tuned spires that burst through the crust in a single breath.

rites.name: Ilovaala
rites.text: Ilovaala is a rite of dark serpents that lash out and bind a living body, pumping it full of altered life-force that lets the bearer wield elemental arts far beyond their training. The stored force runs out and must be restored over time, and only one element can be carried at once. A bound soul may tear the serpent free and drink the surge, swelling their power while reshaping their form, though the swollen body becomes so unstable that a single blow can unmake it.

rites.name: Osumaltanum
rites.text: Osumaltanum is a self-renewal art of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno, in which a practitioner expels a fresh body from their own throat like a serpent discarding its skin. Gravely wounded flesh is made whole, lost limbs regrow, and the discarded shell is left behind to mislead the enemy. The cost is a heavy drain of inner energy, and the most skilled users can shape the new form into something beyond human.

rites.name: Tirakaoma
rites.text: Tirakaoma is a lullaby-shaped technique of the Ki realm, sung by a chorus of hollow-throated beasts once their voices have fallen into unison. Anyone within earshot is drawn into a drowsy waking dream where their limbs and thoughts are wrapped in a sheath of still water. The singers must rest their strained throats for a long while once the chant ends.

rites.name: Tenvanira
rites.text: Tenvanira is a silent surgical art of the Ki realm, in which a healer reads the faint tremors in a patient's life-current, opens a single precise seam, and floods the wound with a gentle tincture that draws the hidden corruption out of flesh and bone. The extracted corruption is then studied and transmuted into a counter-remedy that restores the patient completely. Its practitioners are held in quiet reverence, for the margin of error is measured in heartbeats.

rites.name: Tirataloma
rites.text: tirataloma is a kinetic transmutation that reshapes the user’s dermal matrix into crystalline filaments, which are then expelled as razor‑thin projectiles. each strike fractures the target’s molecular lattice, turning flesh into inert ash in a single impact. the technique is employed by both solitary warriors and siege units, capable of obliterating armored fortifications with a single volley.

rites.name: Meralamira
rites.text: Meralamira is a ritual of coordinated flame and wind practised by the ember-cantors of Ukaraeno, in which a crew seals an enemy into a stone hollow and pours a vast volume of pressed sap across the space. A gust-singer then hurls the sap into a rolling mist while a fire-binder ignites it, turning the chamber into a sealed furnace. The inferno is so hot that everything within it is reduced to ash within a single breath.

rites.name: Suranamari
rites.text: Suranamari is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a practice where a fighter drives their inner vital current to a roiling boil until it vaporises everything it touches. The vapour is stored and released in a single rushing burst that drives strikes and quickens the body.

rites.name: Anasauta
rites.text: Anasauta is a ki-bound memory art in the Ukaraeno powers realm, letting a practitioner quietly log every clash they witness through a drifting spore-like veil. The stored record can only be shared by fusing minds with the listener, so the archive has never been passed around freely. Its keepers claim the whole chronicle of their people sits within it.

rites.name: Kalukanala
rites.text: Kalukanala is a mirror-dancer's technique from the Ki realm in which the caster splits into a crowd of luminous duplicates, each carrying a fraction of the original's vital flame. The duplicates can scatter to confuse foes or fuse back into the caster, returning what they gathered.

rites.name: Anataroma
rites.text: Anataroma is a concept of cloned operatives: a pale fleshy sigil that, once grafted into a bearer's ribs, lets them sprout identical mindless duplicates from their own torso and lend them any technique they have learned. The duplicates hold the bearer's skills but never their will, so the bearer must keep stitching each one back into the body before its strength drains away.

rites.name: Ilolasanari
rites.text: Ilolasanari is a dark spiralling gateway that lets its wielder step between realms he has already located, and anyone who follows him can pass through with little effort. Opening it drains a vast reserve of inner power, and overuse leaves the user unable to call on his deepest eye techniques for a long while afterward. Only a small handful of companions can cross together, and an unseen pursuer may slip through unnoticed.

rites.name: Ilolanari
rites.text: Ilolanari is a shimmering concept of deception in the realm of Ki, a veil of false images that lets a bearer hide among copies of itself. Its illusions endure for ages, and only by shattering the hidden original can the mirage be undone.

rites.name: Kaluvarala
rites.text: Kaluvarala is a rhythm-fire kata of the Ukaraeno's Ki realm, begun by launching an opponent skyward with a sweeping kick. The striker then leaps into a crane-like pose and hammers the falling foe with a storm of blows so swift that they ignite, painting a shimmering crown of flame around the victim. The finished assault drops the target back to earth wreathed in its own burning glow.

rites.name: Anatanmalum
rites.text: In the realm of Ki, the Anatanmalum is a sentient, crystalline entity that crystallizes and amplifies chakra, creating colossal, lion-headed guardians that drain and consume chakra networks. It's a rare and perilous ability, requiring immense control and understanding of Ki.

rites.name: Merakalari
rites.text: Merakalari is a rite of the Ki realm in which a weaver of tidal silence draws the pulse of sleeping stars into a single clay vessel, letting one hollow heartbeat travel across any distance. Its cost falls on the practitioner, who must later sleep for an age to recover from the borrowed rhythm.

rites.name: Meratamala
rites.text: Meratamala is a spirit-sorcery concept in which a practitioner's essence is coaxed loose from the flesh and drifts as an intangible wraith, unbound by blades or flame. Once it finds a host, it can silence the host's inner voice and wear their body like a borrowed coat. Its rivals learned that only a sealed ward of chalk-bound glyphs can hold such a drifting soul before it slips its tether.

rites.name: Osuvanala
rites.text: In the pulsating realm of the Omniverse, the 'Resonance Fist' of the Astral Kin is a spectacle to behold. After synchronizing with the cosmic rhythm, a fist strike sends ripples through the fabric of reality, culminating in a cataclysmic starburst that outshines entire galaxies.

rites.name: Kalutaala
rites.text: Kalutaala is a sealed-breath sensory discipline practised by the Hollow Tidewardens of Ukaraeno, who gaze into the pale resonance of a dying star-lamp. Its adepts learn to shutter their vision entirely and to melt their own tissues into a damping slurry, letting them endure what would unmake any ordinary body.

rites.name: Ukamanira
rites.text: Ukamanira is a breath-borne technique in which the practitioner draws a deep lungful of air and swells back to full bodily fullness, releasing a wave that returns scattered wills to their owners. Those struck regain command of their limbs and mind, yet retain no recollection of the hours they spent under another's sway. It is prized in the Ki realm for its gentleness despite its potency.

rites.name: Osuvanira
rites.text: Osuvanira is a forbidden striking art of the Ki realm, unlocked only when a practitioner has thrown open every one of the body's eight inner seals. The bearer's life force coils into a crimson serpent of fire that propels them across the battlefield faster than the eye can track, ending in a single kick that can erase a foe entirely. The cost is brutal: the bearer's own bones fracture and their body slowly crumbles to ash from the sheer overflow of energy.

rites.name: Osunarira
rites.text: Osunarira is a throwing-star weapon of the Ki realm, its edges wrapped in a living ember that feeds on the wielder's inner stamina. The ember clings stubbornly to whatever it strikes, refusing to be smothered by water, stone, or wet hide until its spiritual fuel is spent.

rites.name: Osuvamsauta
rites.text: Osuvamsauta is a concept in the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse, a sealing-art born in the sixth era that binds an entity's wounds into a single resonant knot. Practitioners weave the knot around a dying body, and the mending is said to take days as threads of living light are stitched back into flesh.

rites.name: Kalulanum
rites.text: Kalulanum is a clay-and-ember construct the Ukaraeno kiln-wardens shape from river silt and fused cinder, sized to whatever task its keeper requires. Its jaws can split a shadow-clone's flesh cleanly in two, and its body shrugs off a detonated reactor core at point-blank range. Keepers stand these constructs in front of their caravans as living bulwarks.

rites.name: Osulamira
rites.text: Osulamira is a Ki-realm technique in the Ukaraeno omniverse that lets a user survive fatal injuries and heal them at once, even briefly mimicking death so skilled physicians are deceived. When fused with Dark Chakra it grants superhuman speed, strength, and renewal, reshaping the body into a younger, heavily muscled form, but losing control of the dark current can tear the user apart from within.

rites.name: Osusaneno
rites.text: In the cosmic ballet of the Zephyrverse, the Harmonic Spiral, a colossal, living tower of crystal and flora, ascends from the planet Elysium, propelled by the synchronized chakra of three elementalists. However, a sudden solar flare disrupts their harmony, threatening the tower's stability and the mission of the climbers aboard.

rites.name: Tiramaari
rites.text: Tiramaari is a sensory art of the Ki realm, practiced by those who learn to still their bodies and open a quiet inner eye. Its practitioners can sense distant flows of energy, read the subtle tremors of a mind shaping its power, and detect when a truth is bent or a false vision is laid over the senses. The art is a discipline of perception rather than destruction, though its masters can unmake a star's worth of concealed strength once they have seen it clearly.

rites.name: Osusamum
rites.text: Osusamum is a concept of two colossal stone formations that rise from the ground of the Ki realm and slam together around a target, crushing whatever lies between them. Its scale can be tuned by how much chakra is poured into its creation and upkeep, from a battlefield-sized wall to a mountain-sized prison. Its wielder regards it as the pinnacle of their earth-shaping art, both for its destructive weight and for how hard it is to sustain.

rites.name: Ilotanamala
rites.text: Ilotanamala is a concept of ceremonial gatework in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, seven ages old, whose roof-tiles conceal chain-driven launchers that loose volleys of keen blades. Its builders forbade firing many volleys at once near the footings, since the stone beneath would fracture and the whole gate would fold inward on itself.

rites.name: Vanamalira
rites.text: Vanamalira is a sealed ember of a fire that cannot be quenched, cultivated by hermits over centuries on a volcanic ridge of the Ki realm. Once it touches any target, the flame devours not only matter but the body's capacity to heal, and no downpour or wind can smother it.

rites.name: Anasarala
rites.text: Anasarala is a resonance technique in the Ukaraeno realm of Ki, taught to young initiates in the sixth era to tune their inner current against the stellar hum. Its first known use shattered the stillness of a dead moon's crater, a display that still anchors the discipline's humility.

rites.name: Tiranalari
rites.text: Tiranalari is a sealing-art technique of the Ki realm in the E6 era, letting a practitioner call forth hidden blades and tools faster than a lightning strike. Its seal-marks hold a vast stockpile of implements that stay concealed until the instant they are needed.

rites.name: Kalunamoma
rites.text: Kalunamoma is a quiet technique of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner's touch lets them lift the weight from another body, leaving it drifting like a leaf on a current. Its masters measure out the amount withdrawn with careful grades, so a single stone can float or a fortress can be left hovering in the air.

rites.name: Ilomaleno
rites.text: Ilomaleno is a concept-realm technique in the Ukaraeno omniverse, in which a gathering of ancient Ki-spirits knots their many lashing tails into one rolling assault. Each spirit contributes its own elemental manner, so the strikes arrive in succession, hammering the target from every angle until nothing remains standing.

rites.name: Anataum
rites.text: Anataum is a silvery concept-metal grown in the hollow lattices of dead star-cores in the Ki realm, valued for how it stores and releases tension. Its most celebrated property is a self-stiffening membrane that can be unspooled across a stellar wind to snare drifting debris and hold it fast. Engineers of the E6 age speak of its web-like reach with reverence and fear alike.

rites.name: Vanatamala
rites.text: Vanatamala is a bone-pale ring-blade of geological strata, grown in the deep quarries of the Ki realm where tectonic pressure once forged the first mountains. Its wielders can split a plate of crust along a fault line with a single slow turn of the wrist. It is said that the blade remembers every ground it has ever cut.

rites.name: Meravaluta
rites.text: Meravaluta is a silent, drifting engine-mind of the Ki realm, built to bear cosmic memory across the sixth era. Its keepers say it once remembered an entire star's death and still carries that grief as a low hum through its crystal lattice.

rites.name: Ukasalari
rites.text: Ukasalari is a root-bound drifter of the Ki realm whose pale, carnivorous shell takes on the faint tint of its own chakra, letting it sink into soil and sap. Through the hidden web of roots and aquifers beneath the land it moves at great speed, vanishing into trunks and dunes alike. Once fused with the earth, its presence blurs out entirely, so that even the most attuned seekers pass it by.

rites.name: Anamareno
rites.text: Anamareno is a sentient gravity-storm born in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a vast spiraling tempest of compressed starlight that drifts between the dying suns of the E6 era. It remembers every planet it has ever swallowed and speaks through the groaning of collapsing horizons. Those who hear its voice are said to lose a piece of their own gravity forever.

rites.name: Anasamala
rites.text: Anasamala is a sealed, thorn-like ember-lattice of crystalline nodes that drift through the ash-fields of Ki, storing residual heat from the Sundering. When fractured by a single disciplined strike, the nodes discharge their stored heat in a single bright pulse across the whole field.

rites.name: Kalunaum
rites.text: Kalunaum is a subterranean stillness-art of the Ki realm, practiced by wardens who sink their intent into the earth beneath a foe. Paired with mirror-shade doubles, a warden leaves a convincing shadow above while the true strike rises unseen from the ground.

rites.name: Vanalareno
rites.text: Vanalareno is a mind-channeling art in the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse, letting a practitioner project memories and emotions across a stretch of spiritual distance. Each added listener drains the caster's body, so long links must be cut short or paid for in blood. Lenses of tuned glass are used by the Orrin Coven to widen the reach.

rites.name: Anakanum
rites.text: Anakanum is a grave-soil art of the Ki realm, in which practitioners draw ground-dust into the dead to rouse them. The lesser form raises endless hollow shamblers that crumble to ash the moment the caster's will lets go, while the greater form restores a single soul-bound body with its full skill, held under a sealed command it cannot refuse.

rites.name: Suranaum
rites.text: Suranaum is a living, shadowy membrane that clings to a host and draws out the host's vital currents, passing them on to others while replaying fragments of memory to whoever it touches. Its hold is weakened by iron-willed hosts who can turn the membrane's own presence against it.

rites.name: Ukaramum
rites.text: Ukaramum is a sigil-bound eye of living ember that hovers wherever its wearer wills it, feeding sight through a thread of inner fire. Its keepers in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno use it both to scout distant ridges and to ignite the sky in a single blinding pulse. Bearing many such eyes at once drains the wielder's vitality swiftly, so only the most disciplined dare the practice.

rites.name: Ukamareno
rites.text: Ukamareno is a concept of mind-binding and life-siphoning within the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, woven through a single branding mark that binds a victim's will and vital current to its bearer. Once marked, a soul can be emptied of memory and remade into an obedient vessel, and their stored vitality can flow outward to whoever holds the brand. The working is said to outlast every attempt to cleanse it from the mind, even by those born with the deepest inner reserves.

rites.name: Tirasanoma
rites.text: Tirasanoma is a sensory discipline in which an invented monastic order of sky-wardens learns to read the quiet resentment and bloodlust that cling to a person like smoke. Practitioners can detect a hidden enemy even when that enemy masks its aura entirely inside a shared spirit-blade, and they can feel the gathering of a wrathful seal long before it cracks. Its masters regard the discipline as a double-edged gift that can turn the reader into the very thing they fear.

rites.name: Kaluvaoma
rites.text: Kaluvaoma is a technique of the Ki realm in the sixth age of Ukaraeno, in which a practitioner discharges their stored lightning through the whole body as a blinding radiance that burns away a target's sight. In the blind moment that follows, the practitioner plants false visions directly into the victim's mind, letting allies strike while the foe sees only what the caster wishes. Several practitioners can weave their radiance together to blind an entire army at once.

rites.name: Tenmauta
rites.text: Tenmauta is a sealed-away technique of the Ki realm, taught to a young disciple by an aging master who forbade its use except in ruin. Every strike opens layers of the practitioner's inner circuits, delivering a cascade of blows faster than thought before a final hammering sends the foe tumbling. The cost is a body hollowed out so completely that the user may never rise again.

rites.name: Ukamalareno
rites.text: Ukamalareno is a sensory illusion technique from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, born from a student's wounded pride after a mentor dismissed its value. It conjures a dazzling false presence that bends the attention of anyone who perceives it, however composed they believe themselves to be. Practitioners treat it as proof that distraction answers to no code of dignity.

rites.name: Suravamira
rites.text: Suravamira is a concept in the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse, a binding lattice of luminous filaments that a wielder lays beneath a target's feet to hold it in place. When many hands weave the same lattice together, the lattice tightens and can pin even a titan-class presence.

rites.name: Kalumanira
rites.text: Kalumanira is a lightning-bound resonance technique in the Ukaraeno omniverse, in which a practitioner's storm-aspected ki sets an object's vibration into a ferocious pitch that lets even a pebble cut through steel. Its power fades entirely if the surge is drawn back before the strike lands, a weakness that duelists in the Ki realm treat as a sacred rule of timing.

rites.name: Ilotanira
rites.text: Ilotanira is a sealed codex of hand-drawn sigils that a nascent realm uses to record the minds of its scribes, binding each page to the reader's memory. When opened in the Ki realm during the third age, its illustrations briefly rewrite the surrounding terrain into the images they depict.

rites.name: Vanakaoma
rites.text: Vanakaoma is a mass-healing rite in which a sentient jelly-mother splits into a swarm of small bodies, each settling onto a wounded soul to carry restorative breath from a caller across any distance. The caller shares the swarm's senses and hears what each fragment finds on the field.

rites.name: Ilokalvanum
rites.text: Ilokalvanum is a cosmic-scale heightened state in the Ukaraeno omniverse, achieved by those who awaken the rare Seerswane eye and channel it through a shroud of pale violet vitality. Its wielders command a cluster of nine drifting sigil-spheres that can be fused into blades, shields, or glowing cages that hold even gods in place.

rites.name: Anasameno
rites.text: Anasameno is a concept-class power in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, letting a practitioner reshape the carbon atoms of their own flesh into a glossy, mirror-dark lattice as hard as cut gemstone. The state can harden a single limb or the entire body, and at full extent forms a shining crystalline shell that multiplies strength while resisting nearly every form of harm.

rites.name: Anakamari
rites.text: Anakamari is a binding technique of the Ukaraeno powers, in which the user gathers a surplus of inner vigor and compresses it into a single hardened core. Its cost is so steep that practitioners must first consume a rare triple-hued elixir to keep their reserves from collapsing mid-act.

rites.name: Surasaneno
rites.text: Surasaneno is a concept of a vast, storm-bright sphere that gathers the shimmering dust of an old wind realm, spun by four radiant limbs into a rotating crown. In the Ki realm of Ukaraeno it is said to be hurled across whole valleys and to split the hardest barriers the sky can raise.

rites.name: Merakaeno
rites.text: Merakaeno is a coordinated battle formation in the Ukaraeno omniverse, in which a heavy-bodied fighter swells to massive size while a shadow-bound strategist anchors their movements. A third member reads the surrounding foes and relays their positions, letting the strike be guided mid-flight with the swing and recoil of a spinning toy on a string.

rites.name: Surasanira
rites.text: Surasanira is a grand ritual-art of the Ki realm in which a painter who has mastered the lesser beast-sketches calls forth towering divine guardians from ink and anger. The guardians grow stronger as the painter's fury rises, able to shatter cliffs and hurl adversaries across open ground.

rites.name: Ilomakalira
rites.text: Ilomakalira is a crimson lattice of sealed chakra, woven by four wardens who stand at the corners of a square and hold its geometry in place. The lattice bends rather than breaks under assault, redirecting the force of a blow skyward before settling back into its original shape, and it can be parted by its wardens to let travelers through. Its cost is such that those who keep it standing can barely do anything else.

rites.name: Anatamlarum
rites.text: Anatamlarum is a dormant resonance woven into the marrow of the Ukaraeno's oldest sky-wells, awakened only when a bearer's inner tide turns dark and grief-hardened. Its power grows with the bearer's reconciled sorrows, and the bearer who learns to channel it must first face the memory of a bond they once trusted.

rites.name: Ukatanraala
rites.text: Ukatanraala is a storm-wrought warlord of the Ki realm who hurls foes skyward on a column of crackling thunder and drives them headlong into the bedrock. Those who survive the descent are rare enough that the wardens of the Ashen Spires keep no record of any who walked away unbroken.

rites.name: Analaroma
rites.text: Analaroma is a sand-born sorcerer-artisan of the Ki realm who, in the fifth age, can mold a dune into a perfect double of any person they have ever seen. The double fights under their command, but they can also unravel it mid-combat and seize an enemy with the falling grains. Within each figure they can conceal powdered star-iron that bursts out when the clone is struck.

rites.name: Suravalari
rites.text: Suravalari is a defensive art of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno's sixth era, in which sealed ward-gates rise from the earth to shield their wielder. Their roof-tiles hide launchers that spit chains of razor vanes, though firing too near the footing can crack the gates' own foundations.

rites.name: Kalutamari
rites.text: Kalutamari is a transformation that reshapes the user into an ocean-dwelling form, with green armored scales, fins, and gills that let them swim at speeds far beyond any land-bound fighter. The scales are hard enough to turn aside blades and can be launched outward as projectiles. Wielders of this form are said to be able to command the sea lanes of an entire coastline.

rites.name: Osuvallaira
rites.text: Osuvallaira is a concept-technique of the Ki realm, in which the wielder's palms wreath an unbroken stream of Ki into hair-fine, razor-edged filaments. Offensively these filaments lash out to sever hundreds of targets at once, down to the tiniest flying insects; defensively they bloom into broad, curved sheets that form an impenetrable lattice around the user.

rites.name: Vanavalari
rites.text: Vanavalari is a race of clay-bodied warrior constructs whose life is bound to a fragile mask, and whose minds are dim but not wholly empty. Born in the deep kilns of a mountain forge, they can sink through soil and drag foes down with them, and their limbs stretch like sinew.

rites.name: Osuralsaala
rites.text: Osuralsaala is a rite-bound storm-technique taught in the high monasteries of Ukaraeno, where an initiate lands five swift strikes before flinging the foe skyward with a crackling uppercut. The practitioner then vaults after the falling body and finishes with a charged thunder-blow to the abdomen that rolls like a summer squall.

rites.name: Anataira
rites.text: Anataira is a bubble-weaving art practiced in the drifting cloud-cities of the Ki realm, where artisans blow shimmering spheres from hollow reed pipes. Each sphere can be seeded with volatile resin that detonates on a whispered word or simply by bursting, and the wisest practitioners can sink a whole fleet inside a single rising globe.

rites.name: Ukaraloma
rites.text: Ukaraloma is a snare-and-burst art from the Ukaraeno powers of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner primes buried clay seals with fire and sends them crawling up a foe's legs. The seals ignite together, cracking stone and scorching the victim to the bone.

rites.name: Tiralameno
rites.text: Tiralameno is a metabolic discipline in which practitioners transmute the stored nourishment of their flesh into a surging vital current, which they channel to swell limbs or their whole frame into monstrous proportions. Novices rely on a bitter triad of tinted tablets that drain the body's entire reserve at once, while masters learn to meter out exactly how much mass becomes power.

rites.name: Osukarum
rites.text: Osukarum is a pyrokinetic discipline of the Ki realm, in which practitioners kindle flames so intense they lift the air into roaring columns that gather into storm clouds overhead. A true master can loose a succession of these blazes in rapid order, and those caught in the cascade may be burned down to fine grey ash.

rites.name: Kalutanum
rites.text: Kalutanum is a rare chromatic sigil-forge inscribed by the Vaelwen smiths of the Ocher Reach, capable of binding a cracked star's ember into a single hand-sized crucible. Its bearer can draw the warmth of dying suns to knit wounded worlds, though no scholar has determined whether it merely strengthens the wielder's gifts or quietly rewrites them.

rites.name: Ilotamrarum
rites.text: Ilotamrarum is a concept of layered sealing, a ward whose anchor markers are scattered across kilometres of marsh so that no intruder can find them quickly. Its hidden grid is tuned to sense any disturbance and answer with a trap that bends the surrounding air and stone. Its reach across Ki is measured in the hundreds of metres, and its counter-measure is a deliberate delay built into the bindings.

rites.name: Kaluramira
rites.text: Kaluramira is a cellular-scale weapon-technique wielded by the mouth-craftsmen of the Ki realm during the fourth age of the E6 era. Its practitioner breathes a living effigy into existence, which bursts and scatters motes that seep into the blood of any who draw them in.

rites.name: Ukamaoma
rites.text: Ukamaoma is a sealed nerve-scrambling art of the Ki realm that sends a crackling current through a foe's own pathways, turning every command the mind sends into a movement it never meant. Only the most disciplined practitioners can recover from it, by painstakingly rebuilding the link between thought and limb.

rites.name: Osulaari
rites.text: Osulaari is a sword discipline from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, whose practitioners strike in the brief instant between an opponent's intent and their first gesture. Its masters can sever a caster's hands before any seal of the Ki arts is completed. The technique is so exacting that its founding teachers measured its quickest strike as a single unbroken moment.

rites.name: Ilokauta
rites.text: Ilokauta is a drifting bloom of mote-fine seed-cells that the Hollow Choir of Ki scatters across the lungs of wanderers to quietly listen to their breath. Its seeds sleep for months until a sudden pressure in the body wakes them, whereupon they swell into a binding lattice that holds the host motionless and drinks their vitality. The stolen vigor can be pressed into another person by a single clasped hand, and the seeds will also bloom as a guard against blows or be violently flushed out when the host draws in a pure tide of Ki.

rites.name: Ukanamala
rites.text: Ukanamala is a concept of a technique-form in the realm of Ki, in which a ki-echo is cast onto a found object so that it appears as a thrown blade, and the true bearer strikes unseen from the flank. Its practitioners in the third age of the era of E6 use it to pair a feint with a lethal follow-up, and the echo can be bound to any spinning mass as well as to a blade.

rites.name: Osumanari
rites.text: Osumanari is a fine iron-dust fighting art of the Ki realm, in which practitioners draw a hidden lodestone grit from the ground and hurl it as a storm of humming pellets. The grains ride a violent magnetic repulsion that accelerates them past the eye, and their sharpened forms can pierce ward-plate and wood alike. Masters of the art are feared most by constructed-automaton makers, for a single grain jammed in a hinge can silence an entire mechanical guardian.

rites.name: Ukatameno
rites.text: Ukatameno is a spiked-sphere maneuver of the Ukaraeno realm's Ki discipline, in which the practitioner's bristling, hardened hair is drawn out and coiled around the body before rolling forward as a whirling thorned ball. Its spikes grow denser and more numerous as the user's training deepens, sharply increasing the rotational force of the charge. It is practiced mainly as a close-quarters breakthrough technique in the late sixth era.

rites.name: Surakanuta
rites.text: Surakanuta is a binding ward-art of the Ki realm, in which three bonded practitioners ring a target with linked fingers and inscribe a hidden sigil that lets them snap through the folds of Ukaraeno to any marked place. Its marks can be set on a single guardian's life so the ring can always return to their side, but its reach shrinks as the payload grows heavier.

rites.name: Anaralari
rites.text: Anaralari is a sonic-illusion discipline in the Ukaraeno realm of Ki, where a practitioner's voice weaves a false reality into the minds of listeners. Its hold resists being pierced by mere awareness, yielding only to a bond of deep affection, and it is wholly ineffective against anyone who cannot hear.

rites.name: Ilokanuta
rites.text: Ilokanuta is a healing-and-binding concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, where a caster offers their vital essence through a thread of pale sapphire light to mend the living or call back the departed. Its cost is strictly borne by the one who weaves it, and a sworn helper may lend strength only at the price of their own final breath.

rites.name: Anatalira
rites.text: Anatalira is a concept of Ki-realm growth, in which living tendrils of pale lumen swell through any opening and expand to fill it with a lattice of woven light. Its practitioners are said to bloom outward from a single seed of will until they can reach or hold something vast.

rites.name: Suratalari
rites.text: Suratalari is a concept of a cage whose floor holds a ring of brass gears that tighten thin, humming filament wound around a captive's frame. Its keeper, a warden named Dresh Vaulan, governs the squeeze by pressing sigils into the air, and he feels each captive's ache as a faint resonance in his own bones.

rites.name: Kalusamoma
rites.text: Kalusamoma is a resonant tremor technique of the Ki realm in the E6 era, which a practitioner projects as a spiralling pressure of vibration. It can be aimed at a living body or at inert matter, where it shakes a target's inner balance until the structure gives way.

rites.name: Ukasanoma
rites.text: Ukasanoma is a lightning-woven gate that a tactician stretches between two points, through which any iron tool hurled into its current is flung with ruinous speed. The method rewards those who can hold the current steady while another guides the throw, and its wielders have long argued over whether aim is a skill or a gift.

rites.name: Ilorareno
rites.text: Ilorareno is a venom-weaving mist-spirit of the Ki realm who must steep a numbing toxin in its marrow for five full cycles before it can exhale. Its breath does not kill but stills nerves, leaving foes frozen while the spirit's bone-hook, the Hollow Sickle, takes its time. It is among the quieter killers of its era.

rites.name: Osurareno
rites.text: Osurareno is a concept of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno universe, a technique that molds ambient moisture into a towering spectral leviathan which the caster hurls forward with a double palm thrust. Its distinguishing trait is that it devours the energy of any opposing technique it strikes, swelling in mass and force with every bite. Practitioners therefore learn to fear fights against masters whose arts are most potent.

rites.name: Ukarannaum
rites.text: Ukarannaum is a binding rite in which two combatants inscribe their sigils upon one another, granting each the power to swap places with the other at any moment of a fight. Its sharpest use turns a wound meant for one fighter onto the hunter who sought them. Scholars of the Ukaraeno chronicles still debate whether the bond is a gift or a curse.

rites.name: Ilonanum
rites.text: Ilonanum is a technique in Ukaraeno's Ki realm, where a practitioner projects bound lattices of ki from their own body to crush and restrain opponents. Its strongest use shatters colossal constructs, while a refined form silences a foe's inner current by locking it in place. The lattices lengthen or shorten at will to match the battlefield.

rites.name: Vanamaleno
rites.text: Vanamaleno is a chakra-forged gauntlet technique woven into the hollow wind-cores of the Ki realm, where wardens of the Hallowed Lattice gather power in their palms and sheathe their arms in it. Strikes are multiplied into a hovering storm of phantom fists that can shatter a fully armored spirit-guardian in a single flurry. The technique is also used defensively, with a shell of spinning fists that repels incoming attacks before the target can react.

rites.name: Meranaleno
rites.text: Meranaleno is a sealing art of the Ukaraeno realm, in which practitioners weave tidal current and borrowed starlight into luminous threads that bind a foe's motion and spirit. It is taught in silence and rarely used, since a bound target's pain is said to leak into the caster's own breath.

rites.name: Ukaranuta
rites.text: Ukaranuta is a sealed resonance of the Ki realm, a lattice of quiet stone-thread that tuned itself to the heartbeat of nearby sorcerers in the third age. Whoever touches its humming core can read the hidden grain of another's inner current and reshape that current into a foreign discipline. Its keepers say the lattice remembers every style it has ever mirrored.

rites.name: Ukalarum
rites.text: Ukalarum is a concussive pressure-art wielded by the Ki-realm's wind-carvers, who channel their breath through hollow reed-bones in their forearms to project a cutting gale. Its force thins rapidly beyond arm's reach, yet at full pitch it can sever a stone column or a standing warrior. The bone-channels are its weakness, for a sealed opening sends the gathered pressure back through the elbows and tears the arms free.

rites.name: Tirasaeno
rites.text: Tirasaeno is a ritual discipline in the Ukaraeno realm of Ki, in which practitioners bind the sky's red resonance into pillars that rise from the ground and hold the world's tension in place. Adepts shift between sealing gestures mid-rite to call these columns or to draw passing workings inward through a sealed throat.

rites.name: Kaluvamira
rites.text: Kaluvamira is a cellular ferment that a Ki-practitioner of the third age can kindle in their own marrow, forcing blood and bone to split and remake faster than death can take hold. Each kindling burns a fraction of the body's allotted divisions, so those who lean on it too often age in a single season. Its masters are called Thresholdwrights, and their hands carry a faint pale bloom that spreads with every mending.

rites.name: Osurakanum
rites.text: Osurakanum is a veil of bent ki that lets its wielder slip out of all sight, a practice passed down in the drifting courts of the Ukaraeno realm. Students learn it first for quiet observation, then for silent strikes that arrive before anyone notices the attacker moved.

rites.name: Anamalareno
rites.text: Anamalareno is a concept in the Ki realm, a rolling cascade of spiraling strikes that folds the air around the wielder into a helix. Practitioners call it a quiet storm because its final blow carries the momentum of a dozen bodies compressed into a single heartbeat.

rites.name: Osutaralari
rites.text: Osutaralari is a mortal-scale hollow-puppet order of the Ki realm, whose adepts restart the hearts of the fallen and wear their faces like borrowed masks. Its practitioners hold that a body remembers the skills it had in life, so each revived husk keeps its old reflexes and martial craft.

rites.name: Tennamira
rites.text: Tennamira is a veil of drifting pale vapor that the Ki-weavers of the sunken valleys summon to bind the air itself. Everything it touches slowly dissolves, yet its wielders walk through their own haze unharmed, a secret guarded by their oath. Three centuries of its use have left the valleys hollow and quiet.

rites.name: Meravarala
rites.text: Meravarala is a concept of drawn-in tidal force, the sea-song of the Ki realm that lets a practitioner call a river's hidden weight up through bare stone. Its adepts strike the ground and the buried aquifers answer, bursting into the open air as a flood that rises from the soil itself. The art is valued for keeping its water unseen until the moment it erupts.

rites.name: Surakarum
rites.text: Surakarum is a sealing-art concept in the Ki realm, a binding that pins a bound being against a host body. The seal is hard to place, and failure can dull the target's movements enough to allow another attempt.

rites.name: Anataruta
rites.text: Anataruta is a soul-binding ritual technique in the realm of Ki, in which a caster channels a fraction of a person's vital essence into a bound volunteer, creating a near-perfect double who answers to the caster's will. The double carries every trait of the original, yet a sharp observer can sense a faint hollowness, and the duplicate fades back to its own form and expires once the borrowed essence is spent.

rites.name: Tenrarum
rites.text: Tenrarum is a sensing veil of chakra-laced grit that its wielder scatters across any ground or drifts through the open air. Whatever crosses its path is silently wrapped in a fine shroud, unmasking even the unseen. It was born in the desert wars of the third age.

rites.name: Ilovarala
rites.text: Ilovarala is a silent weaving art in which a practitioner releases threads of inner current across a field of thrown blades, guiding each one to slip past shields and gather into a single crushing spear. Its masters are said to have once steered a falling moon's worth of shards through a sealed gate of the Ki realm.

rites.name: Tirasaloma
rites.text: Tirasaloma is a sky-binding discipline of the Ki realm, practised by the wind-wardens of the high plateaus of Ukaraeno, in which the practitioner nests five turning orbs of gathered air inside a single cupped barrier. When the barrier is struck, it absorbs the blow and releases the orbs to carry the force onward, bursting into a broad storm-shock on impact.

rites.name: Ilotaala
rites.text: Ilotaala is a concept of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno's third age, a veil of woven hush that drapes a wearer until their surroundings are repeated back over them. Its bearers can slip across open ground, watch a valley for weeks, and strike unseen. Novices are easily betrayed by a mismatched backdrop, since the veil mirrors only what it truly faces.

rites.name: Ilotamuta
rites.text: Ilotamuta is a tide of iron-dust spires that a vast field of lodestone forged across the Ki realm of Ukaraeno during its third age. Its needles sprout in tangled, unpredictable branches, so the surroundings are walled off before the foe can locate a path out, and any touch carries a venom that drains life quickly.

rites.name: Suralareno
rites.text: Suralareno is a ki-woven barrier technique in which a cultivator draws vast quantities of mineral-rich grit into a hovering sheet, then threads living energy through each grain until the whole mass becomes a shield nearly impossible to pierce. Its wardens of the Sahra Vale raise several of these at once during celestial disasters, catching falling cinders in a rippling dune-wall.

rites.name: Anatalari
rites.text: Anatalari is a concept of projected presence in the realm of Ki, where distant minds are cast as luminous, hand-sealed likenesses that shimmer like prisms. Their voices warp and their forms flicker as if struck by static, yet they can speak, act, and turn their borrowed bodies to any purpose. The art belongs to the third age of the sixth era and is used to bridge vast separations between wills.

rites.name: Merasamira
rites.text: Merasamira is a sovereign tide-spirit of the Ki realm, third of its age, who can bind a drowning sky into a single shell of crushing sea-weight. Its ritual gestures call water from the air and the nearest lakes alike, and a bound captive can only be freed when the shell swells past what its walls can hold.

rites.name: Ilosalmaari
rites.text: Ilosalmaari is a veil of drifting grey haze that the Ki realm's dream-weavers use to project hollow shapes which feel real to the mind but cannot touch the body. Hidden watchers slip true blades along the same paths as these shapes, so that the target strikes at the phantoms and is cut by the unseen steel. Over long hunts the veil leaves its prey exhausted and easy to finish.

rites.name: Anasanoma
rites.text: Anasanoma is a sealed ritual-sanctum concept in Ukaraeno's Ki realm, a hollow cavern whose floor is a pool of acid that dissolves any foreign matter cast upon it. Its basalt spires jut from the pool untouched, and anyone drawn within its walls is severed from every companion and left exposed to a slow, inevitable reckoning.

rites.name: Iloramari
rites.text: Iloramari is a silt-bound ward-song carried by the tide-singers of Ukaraeno, who hum it to split rising floodwater around their villages. When sung by a practiced choir it lifts the riverbed on both flanks and funnels any incoming surge away from the singer's path.

rites.name: Kalukaeno
rites.text: Kalukaeno is a seeded contemplative art by which a practitioner draws sleeping potential out of the still water of a sunken temple basin. Each drawn form emerges as a tiny luminous jade bead wrapped in a hum of living light. The art is said to be older than the realm's first lantern-keepers.

rites.name: Kalunanum
rites.text: Kalunanum is a sealing discipline in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno that bypasses personal reserves by drawing on the untouched elements of the natural world. Practitioners bind whole ocean currents, sheets of storm wind, and rivers of molten stone into thin lacquered tokens, which can be unfolded to release their contents on command.

rites.name: Ukaranuta
rites.text: Ukaranuta is a looping wire-trap art practiced in the drifting reed-marshes of the Ki realm, where a practitioner tethers a whirling disc to a hooked weight and lets gravity and tension do the striking. Its masters claim the true art lies not in the throw but in reading where an opponent will step after the first and second arcs. The cord itself is said to hum with the practitioner's breath, carrying a faint charge that can be sent along its length.

rites.name: Tenlanala
rites.text: Tenlanala is a quiet mark-and-leap art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner inscribes a sigil onto anything they wish to reach, then collapses the gap between the mark and their body. Its lore holds that a marked foe is already as good as dead, since the sigil can be called upon at any distance and in any crease of space.

rites.name: Surakalira
rites.text: Surakalira is a ceremonial bronze-and-ember seal-lattice that a monastic order of the Ki realm uses to bind two resonant stones into a rotating storm of breath. Its fourth-age variant lets the bearer launch a hundred sealed shards with a flick of the wrist, each carrying a clinging spark that bursts on impact.

rites.name: Tenlarala
rites.text: Tenlarala is a sealed, slow-brewing engine of ruin in the Ukaraeno realm, a ritual weapon that must first drink in vast stores of ambient vitality before it can be loosed. Its keepers ban it under a standing pact, trading protection for their people's loyalty. Only a being able to swallow its entire charge can ever unmake it.

rites.name: Ukanauta
rites.text: Ukanauta is a discipline of the earth-binding sages, through which a practitioner commands the inert stone, soil and metal of the world to rise, shift and reshape without warning. Its strikes come from directions the eye cannot track, and only searing fire can unbind the enslaved matter and return it to dead rest.

rites.name: Anamarira
rites.text: Anamarira is a ki-realm technique of the third age, a hunting art that conjures ravenous hound-spirits out of the bedrock and sends them after a quarry without rest. Once a hound seizes its prey in its jaws, it can channel the bearer's other arts through its bite, so that the strike lands whether or not the target can dodge.

rites.name: Ukaramala
rites.text: Ukaramala is a concept technique of the Ki realm, a coiled void that opens around the eye of its wielder and gathers whatever lies within its reach into a single point of folded space. Those caught are carried off to a distant resting place, and even substances bound to living energy cannot resist its pull. Practitioners can also send the void through a trusted messenger beast to slip themselves and their doubles away to safety.

rites.name: Analameno
rites.text: Analameno is a binding art of the Ki realm, woven by the Ukaraeno sages for sieges and mass engagements where whole hosts must be held at once. Its practitioners project thousands of ink-shadow surrogates that coil around hostile ranks, and within three seconds each captured form is stained to the bone, locking every limb in place. Once the stain takes hold, no body has ever been known to tear free of it.

rites.name: Suralaruta
rites.text: Suralaruta is a concept that spreads a single ancient gift across seven distinct channels, each granting a different power over force, flesh, mind, life, and the afterlife. Its wielders can answer its divided paths at once, and their strength grows when they work through their own bodies rather than borrowed vessels. Few have mastered its full range, and its origins remain a matter of quiet dispute among the Ki realm's scholars.

rites.name: Ilomamsaira
rites.text: Ilomamsaira is a mind-touching art practiced by the cartographers of the drowned archive, who press a palm to a sleeper's brow to walk the corridors of their remembrance. Veteran readers can race through a week of recollections in a heartbeat, while novices must wade through every hallway, and sealed grief-vaults resist entry for ages.

rites.name: Tiratalari
rites.text: Tiratalari is a dormant reservoir of cosmic tide-force that the Ki realm's third-age ferrymen draw upon only when a sealed resonance-lock is first unbound. Once released, the force can be channeled freely by any trained hand, which is why the Ukaraeno councils regulate its keys so closely.

rites.name: Ukavaum
rites.text: Ukavaum is a planet-sized spinning sphere of condensed Ki that its wielder cradles while three smaller orbiting spheres circle it. On contact, the clashing counter-rotations fuse into a churning vortex capable of gouging a continent's crust. Its wielders are said to be slow to recover even from wounds that ordinary bodies mend in moments.

rites.name: Ilokanira
rites.text: Ilokanira is a concept-class technique of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno, a warding field that bends space so any force touching it is pulled away and deposited at a location fixed by the wielder's mark. Its ability to divert the most destructive blasts makes it the most prized defense of the E6 age's second generation.

rites.name: Anakamala
rites.text: Anakamala is a concept of ki-tempered resonance in the Ukaraeno sixth era, a discipline in which four practitioners anchor themselves to the cardinal points of a sealed valley and hum a shared frequency until the air itself begins to sing. The chorus draws a sphere of violet luminescence that can unmake a mountain range within the span of a single breath. Because the rite depends on four voices held in exact alignment, the loss of any one of them collapses the entire structure before it can ignite.

rites.name: Vanavalari
rites.text: Vanavalari is a living clone technique grown from the body of the Ki-realm wanderer Oselm Tharn, whose spawn cannot be unmade by harm or by the death of their source. Each clone carries a tether to the original and can be steered across great distances, and each can wear the face and power of any being it has touched.

rites.name: Anasanuta
rites.text: Anasanuta is a binding art in which a practitioner must place a target precisely within a sealing sigil, a feat so exacting that artisans craft carved effigies and hollow wooden wardens to guide the placement. Its most famous instrument is a lacquered mask-spirit whose gaze pins whatever it fixes, passed down through generations of wardens.

rites.name: Anasaum
rites.text: Anasaum is a concept in the Ki realm, a binding art in which the wielder steeps blades in personal chakra so that each cut carries a stillness of its own. A pierced shadow locks its owner in place until the blade is withdrawn or the shadow itself vanishes.

rites.name: Vanarauta
rites.text: Vanarauta is a ceremonial geometry of pressure sealed inside the Ukaraeno vaults of the Ki realm, where a bearer locks a foe inside a faceted lattice of condensed will. Tightening the lattice crushes whatever it holds, but a lattice that fails releases a shockwave that ruins the surrounding district and scorches its keeper.

rites.name: Ukalareno
rites.text: Ukalareno is a concept-technique of the Ki realm in the sixth era, drawn into the hands of wandering duelists who gather charged grit into a gleaming shell. The shell can reinforce a single strike or be stretched into several articulated limbs that unleash a rapid storm of blows.

rites.name: Anamaeno
rites.text: Anamaeno is a water-bending concept of the Ki realm in the third age of the sixth era, letting practitioners hold countless suspended droplets that can deflect blasts, ensnare foes, or be sculpted into shifting forms. Its reach extends across great distances, allowing it to call water-born allies into battles that would otherwise deny them any moisture.

rites.name: Osusaloma
rites.text: Osusaloma is a fractured dreamscape-lattice that a Ki-realm weaver folds around a sleeper's mind, pulling their consciousness backward along a moonlit fault line of the world's currents. The traveler may witness the past but can never touch it, and the stay is cut short by an unseen tide that returns them to their own hour.

rites.name: Tirakalnaum
rites.text: Tirakalnaum is a drowsing discipline of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner lulls foes with spores drifting from ancient groves until their minds grow heavy. Those who summon enough inner resolve can still wake, yet the cure lasts only while the afflicted stay raised above the drifting dust or the groves are razed to ash.

rites.name: Ilonanira
rites.text: Ilonanira is a lattice of resonant glass-moss that hums across the drifting skerries of Ukaraeno's third age. Its shell refuses sharp strikes and scatters broad blasts into harmless shimmer, so only force arriving both wide and heavy can break it open.

rites.name: Osumanoma
rites.text: Osumanoma is a binding ward of the Ki realm, pressed over the heart of a chosen bearer so that the bearer can neither end their own life nor peel the ward away. Only a blow driven straight through the chest can sever it, and the strike usually costs the bearer dearly, since the heart is the same organ the ward is holding fast.

rites.name: Ilosarira
rites.text: Ilosarira is a converging technique of the Ki realm in Ukaraeno's E6 era, in which a practitioner splits their spirit into many echoes, each gripping a spinning sphere of compressed ki, then drinks the surrounding ambient life-force to swell every sphere at once. The combined strike has been known to shake even the great beast-spirits of the old border-lands.

rites.name: Vanamarala
rites.text: Vanamarala is a sleeping star-cartographer of the Ki realm, a being whose mind is woven across a chain of orbiting relay-moons. When it wakes, it reads the gravitational song of nearby stars and can redirect their output into a single, devastating pulse.

rites.name: Tenkarala
rites.text: Tenkarala is a Ki-realm sage art in which the practitioner's hair becomes a storm of sharpened needles, grown and hurled in an unbroken stream as the sage gathers living energy into each strand. Its speed and reach are such that only a barrier of solid force can turn the flurry aside, and no evasion has ever been reliable against it.

rites.name: Kalutaum
rites.text: Kalutaum is a binding craft of the Ki realm in which a practitioner draws serpentine wardens from the folds of their robes, each one a coiling intelligence far beyond ordinary familiars. Their scales are said to hold a sovereign grip that no tested wielder of the shadow arts has ever slipped free from.

rites.name: Suralanari
rites.text: Suralanari is a lattice-ward technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner weaves up to thirty-six layered sigils of hardened breath into a sequence of walls. The highest tier of the art can hold back a single bound spirit-host, yet it fails when two such hosts press together.

rites.name: Suranamira
rites.text: Suranamira is a binding-rite that can be sealed into any spirit-beast so that a chosen trigger unlocks a new capacity in it. Its keepers have seen one hound learn to split into a brood, fold its extra heads back into a single frame, rise on new membranous wings, or collapse itself in a final burst.

rites.name: Tensaari
rites.text: Tensaari is a bladed storm-wheel forged by a wandering smith-monk who spins a sphere of compressed gale around her own heart. When she pours more of her inner fire into it, the wheel swells until its glow is visible across distant mountain valleys. Hurled at a foe, it detonates in a gale-sphere that can pin the mightiest guardians of the high realm in place.

rites.name: Vanasalari
rites.text: Vanasalari is a sand-shaped concept in the Ki realm of the E6 era, a grain-bound lattice that holds an entity in a motionless cocoon. Its binding works by keeping the grains in constant reshuffle, so that any defensive reflex or escape route dissolves into the shifting mass. Its wielders can only hold the captive in place until they choose to loosen the grip or end it.

rites.name: Tirataum
rites.text: Tirataum is a flickering illusion-art of the Ki realm that conjures a crowd of mirrored duplicates, each shaped to unsettle whoever watches them most. Its doubles are harmless to touch, but for a few heartbeats they can stop a hunter cold and open a gap for a decisive blow.

rites.name: Anamaoma
rites.text: Anamaoma is a living tide of pale grit that the Ki realm's wanderers call the Drowning Dune. It rises from deep fissures in the bedrock, grinding stone to powder as it crests, and then breaks over whatever stands in its path in repeated surges before settling into a flat, lifeless waste.

rites.name: Tiravamum
rites.text: Tiravamum is a Ki-realm technique of the sixth era in which a practitioner exhales a fine resonant mist that binds to the marrow of foes, letting the caster hurl them backward and then still the flow of their inner energy. Those who bear the residue can be bent into stillness and left open to any strike that follows.

rites.name: Suramalira
rites.text: Suramalira is a resonance art in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, in which a practitioner tunes their inner current to the hum of nearby stone and water. When several practitioners join their tuning, the resonance swells outward, reaching farther and shaking deeper than any single caster could manage alone.

rites.name: Anamaloma
rites.text: Anamaloma is a concept-born thunder-bow forged by the warden of a sealed storm-realm, drawn from nine captured tempests and shaped by an armored colossus of pure will. Its arrow carries lightning strong enough to rival the greatest spinning sphere of wind wielded in that age, though lightning is nominally weaker than wind.

rites.name: Vanasaari
rites.text: Vanasaari is a ceremonial siege-gauntlet of the Ki realm, its forged hand bolted to a wrist-socket that stores pressed vital force. At the moment of loosing, the wrist discharges that force and the detached fist flies across the battlefield with enough impact to crack deep stone, then the wrist draws it home again.

rites.name: Osulanari
rites.text: Osulanari is a veil-weaving craft of the Ki realm in which an adept divides their own breath into shimmering duplicates that stand unseen beside their allies. Each duplicate holds a fraction of the adept's essence, so the more copies made, the thinner the adept's presence becomes. Practitioners of the Ki realm regard it as both a gift and a debt.

rites.name: Osulamvauta
rites.text: Osulamvauta is a faceless colossus of pale jade that wears a ring of small serene visages around its skull, each one a conduit for a different elemental current. Its wielder draws upon all five primal transformations through those faces and can raise a crowd of grasping limbs from the earth to bury an enemy.

rites.name: Tiravaloma
rites.text: Tiravaloma is a concept of Ki-realm poison-thread: a contact-borne toxin that stays dormant until its host bleeds, then bursts the victim outward in a black, swelling detonation. Only severing the flow or sleeping the bearer halts it, and skilled healers can drain the venom to save the afflicted.

rites.name: Ukatamlaeno
rites.text: Ukatamlaeno is a living tidal sentinel of the Ki realm, a shoal-shaped being whose body is a rotating ring of brine that can seal off a drowned basin in an instant. It is most feared for its patience, pinning intruders beneath slowly rising pressure while it waits for them to exhaust themselves.

rites.name: Anavaum
rites.text: Anavaum is a ceremonial battle-dance of the Ki realm, in which a dancer answers a rival's strikes with unpredictable spins, leaps, and blades that appear from unexpected angles. Practitioners are said to strike the nerves of several foes at once, leaving them dazed and open to their own allies. The style is taught only to those who can keep a steady rhythm while surrounded.

rites.name: Kalutaloma
rites.text: Kalutaloma is a ki-realm technique by which a practitioner's body parts into two wholly independent beings with no seals needed, so neither counts as the original. A sealed half cannot rejoin the other, and the split halves the caster's reserves, leaving them unable to sustain heavier arts afterward.

rites.name: Tenraoma
rites.text: Tenraoma is a dormant tidal engine of the Ki realm that siphons ambient stellar heat through hollow crystal lattices and stores it as a quiet, pressurized glow. When awakened, it vents this stored heat in a single cascading release that can rip the skin off a moon's ocean basin.

rites.name: Ilolarum
rites.text: Ilolarum is a ki-realm technique of Ukaraeno's sixth era, a ring of seven spiralling sigils that a warrior etches around a rival's ankles before the bearing lock snaps shut. Its full form has never been witnessed, yet the lone trial left a sky-splitting white bloom that hurled an armoured legion into the mountains. Its practitioners say the circle must be drawn perfectly, and that its heavens are hidden inside the mark itself.

rites.name: Ukatanira
rites.text: Ukatanira is a vast tidal-mantle organism of the Ki realm, able to split its living mass into countless self-sufficient copies whenever a threat presses in. Its reformed body spreads across a whole coastal basin, each portion tending wounds, filtering seawater, or mending the reef beneath it. Its unnamed kin hunt far off, yet every fragment keeps the same restorative will.

rites.name: Ukatanramum
rites.text: Ukatanramum is a fingertip water-pressure technique from the Ukaraeno omniverse, in which a drop is compressed to a needle-thin jet fired at gunshot speed. Its wielders ward off the ocean-wraith kinship of the Ebb-Tide Hollow in the Ki realm of Era E6.

rites.name: Osuvamuta
rites.text: Osuvamuta is a projection-based illusion woven by the Ki-realm couriers of Ukaraeno to hold distant gatherings. Its projected figures appear fully solid, and the caster may reshape the nearby air and stone to match them while watching over the far location through the image. Only a faint ripple sometimes betrays how the caster is moving.

rites.name: Ukavamuta
rites.text: Ukavamuta is a meditative discipline in the Ki realm, where practitioners lay a single drifting petal upon the brow and channel their vital current into it until nothing else in the mind remains. Its masters claim the flawless focus it forges is the true foundation of every great fighter in the age. The petal-crest worn by its adepts is said to descend from the first petal that ever held still under such a gaze.

rites.name: Ukanaroma
rites.text: Ukanaroma is a sealed resonance art in which a practitioner grinds bedrock to a fine dust and steeps it in still water until the mixture stores a slow, tidal pressure. When released through a single held breath, the pent-up tide bursts outward as a shockwave that can split a continent's crust.

rites.name: Ukamareno
rites.text: Ukamareno is a concept of the Ki realm in the third age of the E6 era, named for an invented tide-fire that drinks other beings' inner flames. Its bearers draw out the energy of a foe through a single touch of their lips and can grow stronger with every flame they swallow. The raw fury of certain flames has nearly undone bearers who tried to drink them.

rites.name: Anavalmaum
rites.text: Anavalmaum is a sealed craft that lets a practitioner press their life-current into any substance, after which the work obeys them from afar and can swell or shrink at will. Crafters of the Ki realm say a single infused stone can be made to hold a mountain's worth of stored force, then released as a bloom of pressure. It is a patient art, guarded by the families who first learned to shape the world's fine grains.

rites.name: Ilolanum
rites.text: Ilolanum is a concept in the Ukaraeno omniverse that lets a user split into independent copies, each keeping full strength while sharing one linked mind. Copies grow less clever as they multiply, yet regain wit when others fall, and they cling together by instinct.

rites.name: Suratalira
rites.text: Suratalira is a dreaming current that runs beneath the minds of the great hollow wyrms of Ukaraeno, a shared sea of memory where the beasts speak without chains or sigils. Any mind that drifts close enough to the current, whether bound to a beast or not, may hear its low hum and sometimes answer back.

rites.name: Osukalira
rites.text: Osukalira is a concept of a suspended war-engine that unfurls a veil of thousands of jointed iron filaments from its ribs, each one ending in a hooked claw. Built in the sixth age of the Ki realm, it can sweep a fortress wall clean in a single heartbeat of its mechanism.

rites.name: Osuvanari
rites.text: Osuvanari is a lattice of resonant light-glass plates, grown inside the segmented limbs of ritual constructs, that projects a pale shimmering barrier when its bearer spreads the joints wide and channels inner current through them. The barrier turns aside blows and dispersing fire, though fine powdered ore can creep into its hinges and lock the whole mechanism in place.

rites.name: Ukanasareno
rites.text: Ukanasareno is a sealing ward etched into the root of the tongue that stiffens the whole body of anyone who speaks of a hidden council's dealings. Its lines are said to be drawn from a divination chart, and it dissolves when the one who inscribed it perishes.

rites.name: Osuranala
rites.text: Osuranala is a silver-skinned spirit-weaver of the Ki realm who lives in the shadows cast by tidal moons. Its power swells as the lunar face fills and wanes to almost nothing under a new moon. It cannot abide any lamp or torch, and hides from every flame by instinct.

rites.name: Osumaloma
rites.text: Osumaloma is a drawing discipline from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, where a warrior's blade is unsheathed and lands its cut in a single motion. Practitioners charge the edge with a crackling storm-essence that sharpens it past any mortal whetstone. Its masters are said to sever mountains' roots in the time it takes a heartbeat to pass.

rites.name: Meralaari
rites.text: Meralaari is a crystalline lattice of storm-glass that gathers the ambient sparkle of the Ki realm into a shimmering veil around its bearer. When struck, the veil flares and hurls the stored brilliance outward in a single arcing torrent, while the wearer can still dash forward through the glow.

rites.name: Kaluvamari
rites.text: Kaluvamari is a sealed engine of the Ki realm in the E6 age, a lattice of five resonant crystal heads that bloom in sequence around a vessel-core. Its wardens believe every grief it once absorbed still hums inside it, and its discharges take the shape of whatever sorrow it has most recently swallowed.

rites.name: Tenkaleno
rites.text: Tenkaleno is a concept-realm technique in the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno omniverse, a sealed temporal knot that rewinds a bound person's recent memories into a looping wake. It has never been cast at full strength, because its reversal would unravel the very mind that gave it shape.

rites.name: Kalumaeno
rites.text: Kalumaeno is a dormant resonance woven through the Ki realm's sky-lattice, a silent bell-note that can be tuned to strain any tethered structure. In the Ukaraeno of the sixth era, it is said to be the sound a mountain makes just before it chooses to fall.

rites.name: Osulanira
rites.text: Osulanira is a corrosive mist that its keeper exhales from a sealed gill-vent, dissolving whatever it drifts across within moments. In its liquid form it runs as a river of etching slurry capable of scoring bedrock. Keepers of the Ki realm regard it as a sentinel that devours decay before it can spread.

rites.name: Osuramari
rites.text: Osuramari is a ki technique in Ukaraeno's E6 era, practiced by wandering monks who fold their joy into a single contented breath. When the practitioner laughs fully, the accumulated mirth is released as a rippling pressure that can loosen the bonds of any shrine or structure built on grief.

rites.name: Tenranoma
rites.text: Tenranoma is a binding technique of the Ki realm, woven as a viscous field that pulls at anything touching it regardless of orientation. Practitioners cast it onto ceilings and walls as readily as the ground, so clinging foes sink into the pull and are held fast. Its strongest workings can swallow a fallen star's glow in a single gathering.

rites.name: Merasamuta
rites.text: Merasamuta is a tidal breath technique in the Ukaraeno concept, where a toad-like guardian holds a reservoir of water and expels it on a gust of channelled wind. The stream starts narrow and fast, then fans into a wide flood that retains enough force to shatter hardened crystal barriers.

rites.name: Osukanoma
rites.text: Osukanoma is a quiet-burning sealing art of the Ki realm, taught to apprentices in the third age of the Ukaraeno wilds. Its practitioners press a condensed breath into the air until it folds into a gray, harmless haze that hides them from pursuit.

rites.name: Suramarum
rites.text: Suramarum is a drifting sand-current that the Ki-realm wardens of Ukaraeno use to lift their bodies above the dunes and hold steady in midair. Its glimmering grains are drawn from the iron veins of the far Ashen Teeth, and a single warden can bear a broad raft of them through the sky at speeds that outrun falling stones.

rites.name: Anamarkaum
rites.text: Anamarkaum is a sealed-cell kindling art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner ignites the air of a confined space into a wall of cinder that severs the exit an enemy would flee through while blanketing every other path in burning haze. Its masters teach that a corridor is a sentence and the fire is its punctuation, cutting off one ending while leaving the rest of the text alight.

rites.name: Kalutarum
rites.text: Kalutarum is a tidal-hydric technique of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno omniverse, drawing on the deep ocean pressure that lies beneath the Ebb-Sea of Etra. It lets a single practitioner draw the sea's stored water-mass into an enormous cold surge capable of smothering and quenching vast infernos. The art was formalized in the sixth era of the realm, when wardens began using it to suppress volcanic firestorms.

rites.name: Tiranaala
rites.text: Tiranaala is the primordial rhythm that governs how storm-energy coalesces into spiraling lances of pure discharge. When invoked, it weaves raw potential into a vortex that seeks the path of least resistance through any barrier.

rites.name: Merasanoma
rites.text: Merasanoma is a ki-woven veil technique in which a fire-spirit mimic is conjured from scattered embers that gather into a fleeting double of the wielder. The mimic can carry out small acts of combat for a short while before its ember-threads unravel, though the wielder can reclaim the embers to rebuild it at once.

rites.name: Anasavaroma
rites.text: Anasavaroma is a sword-borne ward of the Ki realm, forged in the third age of the E6 cycle by wandering smiths of Ukaraeno. Its wielder channels gathered stone-light into the blade, strikes once, then leaves a shimmering barrier hanging in the air that devours incoming force. Clashes with rival wardens have repeatedly split high crags apart.

rites.name: Tiramarum
rites.text: Tiramarum is a containment ritual in the Ukaraeno sealing vaults that feeds the dread-tide of an ancient beast into a worn stone sigil instead of extinguishing it. Its shell of pale cocoon-hide and bone-like conduits siphon the creature's power outward while guardian sigils swallow any hostile energy that draws near.

rites.name: Osuvaramira
rites.text: Osuvaramira is a restorative ki-art in which the practitioner's teeth sink into their own vital essence and the wound they leave is a lasting mark of the cost. The art can mend fatal wounds in others and quickly return their strength, but the practitioner's reserves drain fast, so the wise limit themselves to a single use each day.

rites.name: Osuvalari
rites.text: Osuvalari is a veil of silent drift that a practitioner draws across their own being, leaving them without weight, warmth, or any trace the senses or spirit-sight can grasp. Those who master it are said to walk through crowded halls unnoticed, and to vanish from the record of their own kin. The discipline is taught in the lowest cloisters of the Ki realm, where students learn to hold a stillness so complete it swallows even their echo.

rites.name: Vanavarala
rites.text: Vanavarala is a concept of raw earth-bending resonance, a technique in the Ukaraeno omniverse that lets practitioners call up towering stone spires from the bedrock. Its original form requires two users working in concert, while a lone adept can draw a lesser echo that raises several pillars at once.

rites.name: Anatamlaari
rites.text: Anatamlaari is a conceptual weapon of the Ki realm, forged in the sixth era and two ages old, that gathers a wearer's will into a spinning crescent of stellar fire. Its edge is said to sever distance itself, pulling anything it cuts into a folded pocket of space that no one has yet mapped. The Ki scholars regard it as both a tool of defense and a warning about the limits of sight.

rites.name: Anasankarum
rites.text: Anasankarum is a concept of sealed ritual craft in the realm of Ki, in which a bound vessel is laid on a stone table ringed by standing monoliths and an inscribed circle of sigils. Practitioners who draw an inner force from its host risk the host's surge overwhelming the ritual and consuming the operator. Its existence is recorded in the old ledgers of the sixth era, where it is often cited as a warning rather than a method.

rites.name: Merasalum
rites.text: Merasalum is a permanent transformation rite that requires a patterned circle inscribed on the ground before the practitioner forms a sequence of hand signs within it. Shafts of radiant light then wrap each limb and torso, reshaping the body into whatever form and garments the caster envisions, yet the original voice remains unchanged, a telltale trace of the past. Because no known method can undo the change, the rite is treated as a one-way oath of self-remaking.

rites.name: Ilokamoma
rites.text: Ilokamoma is a mind-binding sigil-sequence worked through deliberate hand gestures that steer a victim like a marionette toward a chosen destination. Its mark lies dormant in the flesh for years before a single gesture wakes it, and the afflicted person's irises turn crimson for as long as they remain bound.

rites.name: Ilosarira
rites.text: Ilosarira is a concept of ruinous, self-renewing force in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a green mote that drinks the vitality of whatever it touches and leaves behind only stillness. Its creators bound it in the third age, and it now serves as the deepest weapon of the Wardens of the Ember Tide.

rites.name: Osumakalira
rites.text: Osumakalira is a tidal ki-discipline of the Ukaraeno sea-clans, in which a practitioner draws a current of pressure from the ocean floor and pulls it into a single rising spine. The technique can break open the seabed itself when a master commits fully to the rise.

rites.name: Kalukameno
rites.text: Kalukameno is a concept of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a binding that lets a mind hold a single ember of sunlight within its breath. Its wielders must surrender a few years of life for each great flare, and it can be lost entirely when the bearer's spirit burns too thin.

rites.name: Tenkalmarum
rites.text: Tenkalmarum is a meditative weight-bearing discipline of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner wears a string of prayer beads that slowly shift from pale white through blue, green and yellow before finally glowing red upon mastery. Its purpose is training rather than combat, and whether the beads themselves are essential or any heavy garment could serve in their place remains an open question among scholars of the Ukaraeno powers.

rites.name: Anasalvaeno
rites.text: Anasalvaeno is a drifting veil of charged mist that clings to the ashen highlands of Ukaraeno during the sixth age of the Ki realm. It conducts storm-current so readily that a single sustained discharge can tear it apart and leave the sky clear for days.

rites.name: Kaluvaari
rites.text: Kaluvaari is a binding sigil-ink that, once pressed onto a living mind, reshapes the bearer into a counterfeit of a dread storm-serpent of the deep ocean. The copy inherits the serpent's tidal fury but feeds on the bearer's life-spark, leaving them hollowed and listless while the inscriber holds their will in a silken leash.

rites.name: Analavaloma
