rites.text: Analavaloma is a silver-feathered sky-warden of the Ki realm who keeps the long threads of time from fraying. In its era, it once folded a dying star's final hour into a single breath to buy a city one more dawn.

rites.name: Kaluvaeno
rites.text: Kaluvaeno is a self-sundering sigil-power that lets a bearer tear off wounded lengths of their own lattice and rebuild them into independent sentinels. Its hosts are said to be wardens of the Ki realm, who grow new limbs of the dead reformed into grave-guards.

rites.name: Suravaneno
rites.text: Suravaneno is a coordinated strike technique of the Ki realm's sixth era, practiced by disciples who stand in a line and open the sixth gate together. Their combined aura unfurls into broad luminous pinions as they launch skyward and descend upon a foe. At the moment of impact the enveloping flight contracts into a single edge that can split a massive stony body.

rites.name: Ilotaira
rites.text: Ilotaira is a ring-woven barrier of fire that a Ki-realm warden raises by striking an open palm to the earth, its cylinder of flame drawing strength from the stone beneath. Anyone who touches its outer wall is wrapped in burning light within moments, and the wall holds against blows strong enough to split mountain ridges.

rites.name: Osunamum
rites.text: Osunamum is a sealing technique of the Ki realm in which the practitioner shapes a dense shell of condensed spirit around themselves or an ally, then carves hollow windows into its walls so the wearer can watch the outside world unseen. The shell's thickness and the placement of its apertures are governed by the same breath-discipline, making every opening a deliberate choice rather than a weakness.

rites.name: Osukanoma
rites.text: Osukanoma is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a sustained sonic outburst drawn from a practitioner's grief and channeled through the breath of the chest. Its focused form lets an ally be shielded while the strike is aimed, but the user's inner reserves are emptied in the process, limiting how often it can be called.

rites.name: Anasaari
rites.text: Anasaari is a preparatory weaving of breath and sealed heat that a Ki practitioner exhales into the air before a larger act. Alone it does little, but it leaves the surrounding air primed to accept and amplify whatever fire follows.

rites.name: Suranaluta
rites.text: Suranaluta is a molten-ember armor that a Ki-realm warden wraps around the body, glowing like a cooling forge and searing anything that comes close without a touch. Its heat can be flung outward as a wave that scorches foes from a distance, and it also stands as a bristling shield that discourages blows from reaching the wearer.

rites.name: Anamakaluta
rites.text: Anamakaluta is a silent stillness-art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner gathers pale azure filaments of spirit-thread into a glittering cloud of needles and releases them toward a foe. Each needle lodges in the body and quietly unravels the flow of vital currents, so the victim wastes away over the hours that follow.

rites.name: Iloraala
rites.text: Iloraala is a pale, sweet-scented bloom that grows in the highlands of Ukaraeno, where its perfume gathers in the hollows of valleys. Those who breathe it are shown the memories they most wish to forget, and the resulting despair can hold a traveller in place until they wander off a ledge. Its scent lingers on cloth and keepsakes long after the flowers are gone.

rites.name: Suratansaum
rites.text: Suratansaum is a fire-breathing kindling art of the Ki realm, practiced by those who knead inner ember in the belly until it can be exhaled as a widening tongue of flame. Practitioners of the Ukaraeno sky-forges pair their breaths into a single rotating firestorm that can boil lakes away within moments.

rites.name: Tiramaroma
rites.text: Tiramaroma is a sphere of gathered moonlight that its wielder spins into a dense swirl of pale violet fire, its radiance crowned by a white crescent holding a single star. Forged in the third age of the Ki realm, it is said to be a technique passed down among wandering healers who use it to cleanse blighted ground. Its bright edge can split stone and quiet raging spirits alike.

rites.name: Anakalari
rites.text: Anakalari is a sealed relic of the Ki realm, a crystalline lattice that hums when a bearer's breath matches its resonance. Its keepers once used it to split drifting moons of frozen rock into navigable halves for the caravans of Orrin's Drift.

rites.name: Vanarameno
rites.text: Vanarameno is a sealing lattice of woven spirit-threads that its keepers raise as a hemispherical dome to absorb and stall catastrophic bursts of force. At its keeper's word the dome parts cleanly along its midline, releasing whatever it has held.

rites.name: Vanakamoma
rites.text: Vanakamoma is a tidal current of stormwater that rises from the lagoons of Ki each sixth season, pulling loose timber, bells, and lantern-glass into its spiral. Its tide-wardens can knot the drifting debris into a single barrier that holds back even a flood of the strongest kind.

rites.name: Tiranauta
rites.text: Tiranauta is a shapeless tide-spirit of the Ki realm that sheds its own mirror-slick membranes like a river discarding ice, leaving behind shimmering husks that hold its memories and mimic its form. Its trails of silver residue are said to be able to drown sound and sight alike, so that the sleeping lowlands of E6 remember only a faint wind when it passes.

rites.name: Osulanuta
rites.text: Osulanuta is a last-resort surgical art of the Ki realm, in which a healer tunes every cell of a dying patient to vibrate in unison with their own refined spirit-current. The stimulated body mends torn flesh and fractured bone even as the healer works, buying a few precious percentage points of survival in hopeless operations.

rites.name: Ilotamira
rites.text: Ilotamira is a sheet of living iron-dust that its keepers raise into a standing barrier when the sky above their quiet valley turns hostile. Each grain answers to the will of its wielder, so the wall can be thickened, bent, or hardened to meet whatever is coming. Walls of this kind have held against storms that would have flattened stone fortresses in the same age.

rites.name: Kaluvarira
rites.text: Kaluvarira is a sinking technique of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner descends bodily into the ground or a nearby surface, each measure of depth drawing pain and wounds into the flesh. Its only release is the practitioner's own will, and it ends the instant they cease to breathe, so it serves best as a binding delay rather than a lethal blow.

rites.name: Tirakamala
rites.text: Tirakamala is a tidal current of ki that lives in the deep seams of Ukaraeno's third age, where drowned bells ring underwater. Its keepers can gather the resonance of the sea floor and hurl it upward as a single pressure wave that breaks mountains and drowns whole valleys.

rites.name: Merasamala
rites.text: Merasamala is a concept of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a tidal serpent of storm-charged brine that coils through the sky before striking. Its power lies in the way it stuns whatever it touches, locking muscles so that foes stand helpless before the next blow.

rites.name: Tenkansarum
rites.text: Tenkansarum is a mechanical weapon-body carried by the sentinel-engineers of the Ki realm in the sixth age of Ukaraeno. When its limbs are unbolted, the detached segments unfold into a swarm of ember-tipped projectiles that can blanket a valley or hunt a single heart across the sky.

rites.name: Ukatannamum
rites.text: Ukatannamum is a collective binding art in which a circle of practitioners weaves luminous filaments of hardened light across a single target, and each added hand multiplies the grip until even a veteran is pinned in place. Its strength is in numbers rather than in any one weaver, and the Ki realm's eras have seen it used to hold back storms of Chaos-born beasts.

rites.name: Suralaoma
rites.text: Suralaoma is a concept of a deflecting ward woven from hardened resonance, able to turn aside both physical missiles and arcs of channeled spiritual force. Its practitioners in the Ki realm describe it as a mirror that bends whatever is thrown at it back along its own path. It has been recorded holding against blows of considerable power.

rites.name: Osuraltaala
rites.text: Osuraltaala is a dual-wielded ki technique of the Ukaraeno concept realm, in which a bearer splits a violently spinning sphere of compressed force into two blades that tear through even the hardest living hide. Its edge is sharp enough to sever the thickest armored limbs of titanic beasts in a single pass.

rites.name: Osumanuta
rites.text: Osumanuta is a compacted spinning core of gathered force, forged by a practitioner who folds a second palm over the first to crush the sphere past safe limits. It slips through barriers that would stop ordinary strikes and can drop colossal foes even when the blow is softened, yet the crushing bends the wielder's arm, so each use costs them dearly.

rites.name: Osunamira
rites.text: Osunamira is a storm-tempered warrior of the Ki realm who draws raw lightning from a dormant ember in her chest and compresses it into her knuckles. Her signature blow arrives faster than thunder and has been known to tear through barriers of living sand before hurling its target through stone walls.

rites.name: Osunanoma
rites.text: Osunanoma is a concept of hardened stillness, a principle held by the Ki realm that a thing's resistance and its momentum can be made one and the same. Those who attune to it can lend a sliding weight its full force until frame and rail give way beneath it.

rites.name: Anamaramira
rites.text: Anamaramira is a stitching art by which a practitioner draws on a self-renewing wellspring of inner current to knit shattered vessels back together and reseal the single hidden seam where their core lies open. While the wellspring holds, its wielder can outlast wounds that would end any other life, though a dry spring leaves them as mortal as anyone.

rites.name: Suravamoma
rites.text: Suravamoma is a shifting lacquered shell worn by the mystic-warriors of the Ki realm, able to reshape its wearer's bulk and features like a theatrical mask. Each reshaping, however, drags the wearer's mass heavier, turning every disguise into a burden on speed.

rites.name: Ilosavaneno
rites.text: Ilosavaneno is a storm-wrought sovereign of the Ki realm, said to be forged from the first crack of a dying sky and sheathed in a blade of coiled lightning. Its strikes rend the air into burning ribbons, and its presence is felt as a rolling pressure that bends weather for leagues around.

rites.name: Kalusaeno
rites.text: Kalusaeno is a sensing art practiced in the Ukaraeno omniverse, where the wielder frames the world through a hand-shaped lattice and reads the inner glow of every living soul in sight. Its practitioners can widen their reach by scattering their essence across distant reeds that drift and listen on their behalf.

rites.name: Ilovarira
rites.text: Ilovarira is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a veil of drifting luminous motes that masks the wielder from sight while leaving them fully aware of the world around them. Its strike is delivered through the shimmer, so the blindness it imposes on foes does nothing to dull its edge. Few in Ukaraeno have mastered the concept, since its perfect concealment depends on a nearly flawless control of ki.

rites.name: Ukasauta
rites.text: Ukasauta is a resonant hymn-technique of the Ki realm, said to have been composed in the third age of the E6 era by a wandering singer who tuned the wind to the pitch of distant storms. Practitioners chant it while spinning a sealed spiral of air, and the bound pressure can split stone in a single breath.

rites.name: Vanakanuta
rites.text: Vanakanuta is a dormant snare woven from unseen barrier seals, each hidden in ordinary terrain until something unaware steps within its reach. Once triggered, it swells into a crimson sphere that squeezes, swallows and grinds whatever it holds before shattering apart like cracked glass when broken.

rites.name: Tenraloma
rites.text: Tenraloma is a sealed clutch of parasitic hatchlings, each the size of a grain of sand, kept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno's sixth era. Once released as a cloud, they burrow into a host and feed on the chakra being spent, and the more the host burns, the faster they ripen into a detonating brood.

rites.name: Vanavamum
rites.text: Vanavamum is a concept of the Ki realm's E6 era, a bladed whorl of condensed spirit-current spun between the fingertips of a wandering mender. Its edge is so fine that it severs the rooted hollow-kin of the far marshes with little resistance, though its reach is far smaller than the vast storms of its kind.

rites.name: Tenvaari
rites.text: Tenvaari is a concept-realm entity of the Ki realm, cultivated in the drifting mid-layers of the Ukaraeno omniverse during its third age. In youth it swells as a vast, translucent froth that smothers whatever drifts too near, and in maturity it hardens into a crystalline sphere that swallows intruders into an endless mirror of their own recollections.

rites.name: Vanakaloma
rites.text: Vanakaloma is a concept of black ignition that a sovereign of the Ki realm draws from the hollow of a single eye, where the flame burns only where the gaze settles. It is named for the ember-father of forge-gods in the old tongue of Ukaraeno, and no living scholar has seen its flames gutter out until the dawn-chime of the Seventh Cairn.

rites.name: Osusaoma
rites.text: Osusaoma is a dormant spore-cloud of the Ki realm that drifts through still air, settling on wanderers' skin and weaving a looping perception that keeps them retracing the same path. Its victims feel the loop as distance, though they stand motionless in the drifting haze. Dispelling it requires scratching a visible sign into the loop, after which the spell unravels at once.

rites.name: Tiralaroma
rites.text: Tiralaroma is a dark, ink-like concept that the people of the Ki realm use to draw life-force out of an opponent and bind it into their own limbs. It can be worn as a mask over another's form, but a careful observer sensing for subtle tremors in the stolen pattern will see through the disguise.

rites.name: Kalutaala
rites.text: Kalutaala is a concept of a binding ritual in the Ukaraeno realm of Ki, where the practitioner's breath is folded into a spiraling gale that can blind a rival or flatten the land within reach. Stretched by sustained will, the same storm can be widened until it blankets a whole island under a single turning sky.

rites.name: Ukamaluta
rites.text: Ukamaluta is a veil-woven rite of the Ki realm in which a practitioner conjures a gargantuan spirit-double that rises from the ground beneath a foe. The double then seizes the victim, hurls them skyward, and binds the illusion to collapse at the moment of impact.

rites.name: Ukasaleno
rites.text: Ukasaleno is a silvery spiral of condensed starlight, born when a warden of the Ki realm cradles a sphere of truth-sight in its palm and releases it. The storm it unleashes can split the crust of a moon, rivalling the greatest spinning sphere ever forged by a rival warden.

rites.name: Tenlarnalum
rites.text: Tenlarnalum is a sealing array of paper-like wards that its maker scatters over a chosen ground, each one humming with stored binding will. At a single gesture of the hand the wards fold inward and lock any living thing within their ring in place, leaving it helpless before an ally. The maker can unseal the wards at will, releasing the captive without a trace of harm.

rites.name: Ukavaala
rites.text: Ukavaala is a chorus-sealing rite in which eight voices lift their hands in one shared gesture to bind a storm-spirit at the heart of a lattice of silver threads. Its hold is brittle: a single unbroken cry from the bound spirit can scatter the whole circle before the knot closes.

rites.name: Suralaoma
rites.text: Suralaoma is a nerve-sealing art in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, practiced by monks who strike a single hidden point on an opponent's body to keep their inner tides from rising. Its wielders can quiet a foe's bodily reserves at the very moment they prepare a crushing burst of power, leaving the enemy unable to ignite it.

rites.name: Merakaroma
rites.text: Merakaroma is a hardened-filament thrust technique, drawn from the hair of Ukaraeno's Ki-realm engineers, that fires a dense volley of needle-thin shards capable of pinning a ward-shield or a rival's flight mid-air. Its practitioners lock a foe's kinetic channels with a single well-placed needle, freezing them in place for the length of a breath.

rites.name: Ilovaeno
rites.text: Ilovaeno is a sealed resonance art of the Ki realm, practiced by paired adepts who weave their breath into a shared lattice of folded light. When several practitioners align their folds, the lattice amplifies each member's output far beyond what any single hand could reach.

rites.name: Ilosamala
rites.text: Ilosamala is a sealed-circle technique in the Ukaraeno omniverse that draws a bound space around a target and slowly tightens its walls until the enclosed body is pressed to nothing. It is taught in the Ki realm of the third age as a means of isolating a single foe from the rest of their companions.

rites.name: Vanataari
rites.text: Vanataari is a concept of a deep-diving amphibious sealing-art, the flesh-pocket of a vast marsh-wyrm that drinks silt from the bottom of sunken lakes. Within its gut lies a membrane that scrambles the sensing of anything that seeks it by vibration, heat, or spirit. It is used by couriers and saboteurs who must pass through guarded shorelines unnoticed.

rites.name: Kalunamari
rites.text: Kalunamari is the rule that any practitioner may draw strength from a flowing current of ambient spirit called the Ryūmyaku, but only the sovereign's blood may stem that current or let it run again. The concept fixes who holds the tap, not how much the river can carry, so every bloodline of the crown guards its own sealing rite.

rites.name: Ilokanoma
rites.text: Ilokanoma is a sword-drawing art practiced by the wandering blademasters of the Ukaraeno's Ki realm, who believe a single clean stroke can sever any bond. Its practitioners draw and sheathe in one breath, and the strike is said to cut through the spiritual anchor of any creature, however vast.

rites.name: Vanalamum
rites.text: Vanalamum is a rolling storm-wall of compressed Ki that its wielder drives into foes in a rapid chain of detonations. Each pulse is wound from layered spiral currents, so a single strike can split a battlefield open. Its wielders call the technique the cascade of drowned suns.

rites.name: Ukasalari
rites.text: Ukasalari is a tidal-binding discipline in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, in which practitioners fold the pressure of distant seas into a single crushing stillness that pins an opponent in place. It is taught in the third age of the E6 era as a means of holding ground without striking.

rites.name: Osunansaum
rites.text: Osunansaum is a sealing-breath technique born in the Ukaraeno age E6, when a cave-ins threatened to bury a company of warriors beneath a mountain. Its user, Ayawaru Tenkōshi, pressed a spinning sphere of compressed ki against the rockfall and the blade at his hip answered his despair with a surge of borrowed force. The technique remains taught mainly as a lesson in how emotion can reshape a weapon's nature.

rites.name: Kaluvaneno
rites.text: Kaluvaneno is a sphere of compressed resonance that its wielder can call into being at once, with no gathering or charging stage needed before it takes shape. It was devised in the youthful era of the Ukaraeno powers as a counter to the slow, telegraphed spheres that rivals relied upon.

rites.name: Ilonarkalum
rites.text: Ilonarkalum is a sealed pocket-realm of drifting tidal glass, accessible only through a soap-bubble rift that its keepers open to slip out of notice. Within it, a patient guardian can wait for centuries before choosing the moment to step back into the world. Its walls have been tested by hunters who sought to lock the guardian inside permanently, and they have always given way.

rites.name: Ilovaluta
rites.text: Ilovaluta is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a reflex that conjures an earthen double to absorb a blow aimed at its user. When the double collapses, its mud hardens around the attacker's limb, binding it while cursed seals spread across the rest of the body, though a sufficiently stubborn will can tear free.

rites.name: Tiramanum
rites.text: Tiramanum is a slow-acting mental binding worked into the skin of a target, spreading as its hold on the mind deepens. Its bearer must renew the mark regularly, for when it fades the buried recollections return in a splitting ache. The Ukaraeno Ki-realm's courts have long valued it for quietly rewriting what a person chooses to remember.

rites.name: Tenramtaum
rites.text: Tenramtaum is a sky-born siege engine of compressed dust that its wielders raise over the Ki realm's desert plains, gathering grains into boulder-sized weights that fall like judgment. Each stone is aimed to cover a wide field, leaving no lane of escape for those below. The fall itself also serves as a feint, drawing attention skyward so that a second strike can rise unseen from the ground.

rites.name: Anaranum
rites.text: Anaranum is a concept of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno omniverse, a shimmering lattice of mirrored breath that can split itself into echo-forms from palm-sized to full human stature. Its duplicates are tough enough to shrug off crystalline wardings and blades alike, and the concept is said to be three ages old.

rites.name: Tenlamarala
rites.text: Tenlamarala is a mirror-weaver of the Ki realm who bends the moisture hanging in the air into a silvered lens that turns back whatever strikes it. Her craft falters under open sun, when droplets boil away into nothing, and a sudden blaze of white light can blind her and collapse the reflection entirely.

rites.name: Tiratanum
rites.text: Tiratanum is a standalone sealing technique of the Ki realm, a pressure-strike that folds an opponent's flowing energy back into their own meridians without needing any prior parry or reversal. Its practitioners are said to have sealed whole tidal storms in the Ukaraeno age of the Sunken Vellum.

rites.name: Anatalum
rites.text: Anatalum is a stance-born discipline from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, where a practitioner draws a sphere of compressed tidewater between cupped palms and fires it through a finger frame. Each volley is released as a cascade of pressurised droplets that strike with the force of a stone thrown by a siege engine.

rites.name: Kaluramuta
rites.text: Kaluramuta is a sustained water-binding art in which a practitioner draws a long-lived tide-serpent from a dyed fountain and braids it to their gaze, so every current and ripple becomes a set of eyes. The art drains its user steadily, and the longer the serpent lives, the heavier the fatigue settles on the caster's bones.

rites.name: Tennamum
rites.text: Tennamum is a quiet, bone-deep stillness that sits beneath the Ukaraeno's thin crust of ordinary physics. Its wardens claim it is the first pulse that taught the cosmos to remember its own shape. Those who wake it describe a warm pressure that bends memory like wax.

rites.name: Tenlaoma
rites.text: Tenlaoma is a tide-bound lattice of coiled serpent-spirits that drift through the shallows of the Ki realm, each one carrying a fragment of a drowned sun's memory. When the tide turns, the spirits unwind into a spiraling funnel of living current that can pull a whole coastline into its throat.

rites.name: Anavatanira
rites.text: Anavatanira is a siphoning art of the Ki realm in which a practitioner draws the inner vitality of a rival through a bond of touch and breath. The stolen force can be spent as one's own, though a body that cannot hold it begins to harden into stone or split at the seams.

rites.name: Vanasauta
rites.text: Vanasauta is a warding current that flows through the bonds between kin in the Ki realm, binding their fates so that harm to one echoes through all. In the E6 age it is said to have once steadied a collapsing mountain range by sharing its strain across a hundred living hearts.

rites.name: Ukavauta
rites.text: Ukavauta is a concept, a technique of the Ukaraeno universe's Ki realm, in which a practitioner draws metal-laced grains from the terrain and bends them into a living storm. The grains rise into a lattice of shards that orbit the wielder before collapsing into a single crushing lance aimed at the ground beneath an opponent.

rites.name: Kaluvamuta
rites.text: Kaluvamuta is a mental art practiced by the Ki-realm seers of the Ukaraeno, who trace silent sigils across the iris so that a watcher's thoughts drift loose into their hands. It can slip beneath the guard of a mind already prying into one's own, and turned inward it lets the practitioner unpick, mend, or erase the threads of their own remembered past.

rites.name: Merataneno
rites.text: Merataneno is a dome-shaped ward woven by a circle of guardians who stand at its edges and offer their own spirit as the anchor. The ward admits anyone who approaches with open intent, yet it holds fast against anything that would cross it with malice or raw force.

rites.name: Ilovaruta
rites.text: Ilovaruta is a concept-realm construct, a hollow lattice of crystallized intent that exists only while someone remembers its purpose. It can sever the ties between puppets and their wielders across the Ki realm, and it is said to fold a battlefield into a single held breath.

rites.name: Tensamvanum
rites.text: Tensamvanum is a field‑manipulation rite that warps the olfactory field of a combatant, allowing them to project a fleeting, scent‑free mist across the battlefield. The mist, a lattice of micro‑vortices, temporarily erases the target’s scent signature, rendering them invisible to scent‑based detection. Though harmless to the user, the mist can be deployed in swarms to disorient foes and mask the wearer’s presence.

rites.name: Osusanira
rites.text: Osusanira is a dark-chakra strike in which the wielder compresses shadowed energy into a sphere ringed by two orbiting bands of void, then drives it into a foe's body. The impact is said to fracture bone and split the air around the blow, leaving the target hollowed by a force that gives no warning.

rites.name: Vanavaum
rites.text: Vanavaum is a sky-threading duelist of the Ki realm who moves by slipping between heartbeats rather than through space. Their stance is a silent glide that leaves afterimages drifting like loose kites, and rivals swear they have struck the same spot twice in one breath. The Ki elders consider the technique a gift that is also a debt, for every instant saved is paid back in the stillness of the surrounding air.

rites.name: Anarauta
rites.text: Anarauta is a whirling discipline of the Ki realm, taught in the Ember-Spire orders of the E6 era, in which the practitioner spins through a crowd while channeling vital force into a ring of lightning-bright arcs. Its name means 'the dancing circle' in the old tongue of Ukaraeno, and the masters claim it can unmake a wall of foes in a single revolution.

rites.name: Analamira
rites.text: Analamira is a sun-scarred wind concept from the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a discipline of drawing the breath of storms into a lattice of razor currents. Practitioners weave these currents into a vast cutting web that shreds whatever stands within it, rock and foe alike.

rites.name: Osumannaala
rites.text: Osumannaala is a resonance-based counter-force in the Ukaraeno powers system, a sonic current that unmakes crystalline growth by shaking it apart at its own atomic rhythm. Its practitioners are rare and sought after by those who fear the spreading lattices of their rivals.

rites.name: Vanavamari
rites.text: Vanavamari is a nested illusion-engine that sits in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno, a sealed concept-lattice where every fabricated copy is more real than the original. Its signature is a gallery of clay-sculpted doubles that, when detonated, scatter motes which unmake anything breathing them. Vanavamari is named for the sculptor-deceiver who first mapped how a false sight could be weighed as truth.

rites.name: Suramareno
rites.text: Suramareno is a ceremonial rite-sigil of the Ki realm in the Ukaraeno, a formation of woven ember-threads that a bearer lights to sharpen reflexes and reach. Its keepers trace it across the air in the ninth dawn-hour to call down a column of dark-gold flame that rises as a forest of burning spires.

rites.name: Kaluralira
rites.text: Kaluralira is a cutting art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner threads a thin current of storm-bright energy along a blade of bone-steel and then answers with a rapid, scattering flurry of strikes. It draws on little reserve and needs no inherited sight, though its reach falls short of the grander arts of its lineage.

rites.name: Vanamalum
rites.text: Vanamalum is a black-violet ember that drifts through the ashen plains of Ukaraeno, feeding on the regret of those it touches. Its heat does not merely burn flesh but seizes the will, bringing a runner to their knees before they reach the one they hunt. The wardens of the Ki realm have sealed it in glass lanterns to keep its hunger from spreading.

rites.name: Ukalamsauta
rites.text: Ukalamsauta is a concept in the Ki realm of Ukaraeno's third age, a technique that lets a wielder sheathe their whole body in layered carbon lattice plating, shifting its colour between two tones as the armour forms. Its wearer can also crystallise the knuckles into a dense hardened lattice for a single decisive strike. The sages who record it warn that the plating locks breath and rhythm, and that its weak point has never been fully mapped.

rites.name: Tenvanala
rites.text: Tenvanala is a concept of the Ki realm in the sixth era, an invented sigil-current that tightens around its target like a hungry fist before bursting outward in a dense flash. It is wielded by sleeve-borne shadow-weavers who treat the blast as a sealed exhalation rather than a fire. The current is said to swallow stray light whole before releasing it all at once.

rites.name: Ilokamira
rites.text: Ilokamira is a stored-resonance technique of the Ki realm, in which a blade is driven into bedrock so that each cut etches a sigil into the stone that holds its flow. The final detonation discharges every sigil at once, releasing a compressed burst of spirit-force across the battlefield.

rites.name: Surasanoma
rites.text: Surasanoma is a concept of Ki in the sixth era, a technique in which a practitioner splits off a duplicate of their own motion to launch the original like a spear. The act appears throughout the realm's duelists as a way to close a gap faster than the eye can follow. Its strikes are measured in the stored force of the launch, not in any sustained burning.

rites.name: Vanavamuta
rites.text: Vanavamuta is a storm-spirit of the Ki realm who coils the high pressure fronts of the sky around her body until they howl like caged animals. She then kindles the charged air into a rolling sheet of blue-white fire that can strip the surface of a moon. Her power is said to be most dangerous at the moment the winds first begin to catch.

rites.name: Ilokantaeno
rites.text: Ilokantaeno is a ritual of sealed lamp-glass tempered in the ashes of old suns, wielded as a wielder's inner flame made visible. Its practitioners strike three resonant strokes that split the target's reckoning, then loose a drifting veil of luminous dust that detonates into searing heat when it settles.

rites.name: Surakanira
rites.text: Surakanira is a silent cadence of ember-chant practiced by the Ki-wardens of Ukaraeno's sixth age, who draw a shimmering edge of kindled air and let its heat roll outward before them like a tide. The working collapses the instant the wielder's focus breaks, so the wardens train until sleep itself cannot pull them under.

rites.name: Kalunareno
rites.text: Kalunareno is a lightning-binding discipline practiced by the storm-shepherds of Ukaraeno's sixth era, who gather charged air into a crackling orb that drifts over a foe before loosing a rain of white-hot strikes. The technique is said to have been codified after a single sky-scouring storm reshaped the continent's eastern coast.

rites.name: Osutavanira
rites.text: Osutavanira is a wandering clan of ancient off-world cultivators who travel from planet to planet tending towering seeds of living light, then harvesting their luminous fruit once the indigenous peoples have been erased. Their most fearsome members can sunder crust and stars alike, and their crown achievement is a fruit-bearing tree whose roots hold a whole world in thrall.

rites.name: Meralauta
rites.text: Meralauta is a sealed archive-cathedral in the Ki realm where keepers listen to the dreaming memories of fallen seers and sort them into tide-charts for the coming age. Its archivists are said to have mapped the courses of wandering stars through the echoes left in human recollection.

rites.name: Tentamum
rites.text: Tentamum is a clandestine interrogation corps of the Ki realm, founded three ages ago to pry secrets from captured fighters and turncoats through the mind and the body alike. Its operatives are trained to read a prisoner's breath and tremor as carefully as a scholar reads a manuscript.

rites.name: Merakaoma
rites.text: Merakaoma is a sanctuary-hospital in the Ukaraeno realm of Ki, where healers of the Vorrun Circle mend wounds through shared breath and borrowed warmth. Its founding physician trained a generation to stabilize armies in the midst of collapse, and later stewards widened its wards into a network spanning every district.

rites.name: Anasanira
rites.text: Anasanira is a dormant ritual-engine built in the deep tombs of the Ukaraeno realm, meant to bind the restless spirits of the fallen into a single chorus of obedience. Its keepers claim it can animate a whole host of the long-dead, each bearing the skill they had in life, to march again under a single hand. Whether it still answers to anyone is a question the ruins have not yet settled.

rites.name: Ilosauta
rites.text: Ilosauta is a veiled legion of several thousand clockwork sentinels, each animated by a lens of pale sight that can see the hidden seams of matter. Its commander rules from a floating citadel built from a dead satellite of a sun-cold world, and the legion marches only when the stars align over their chosen target.

rites.name: Kalusamum
rites.text: Kalusamum is a resonant lattice of chilled glass that hums through the Ki realm, storing the breath of dead stars in its ringing hollows. Ukaraeno's third age knew it as the Quiet Anvil, a substance that could bend the ambient pressure of entire seas when struck. Its song is said to outlast the cracking of the frost it was made from.

rites.name: Ilovamuta
rites.text: Ilovamuta is a dormant, many-limbed chthonic colossus of the Ukaraeno, sealed by the Ki realm's sacred geometry inside a pocket of folded dark where only the wardens of the Ashen Lattice may walk. Though young, its hunger for the ambient heat of worlds makes it a catalyst for any siege that dares to wake it.

rites.name: Amaularnia
rites.text: Two allies combine their inner energies into a shared spinning sphere that strikes a foe. The technique then merges with a colossal beast-form, launching a swirling orb that detonates on impact.

rites.name: Valeonanum
rites.text: A combined assault in which two fighters summon colossal spirit forms, one striking with a blade while the other fires a massive sphere of energy. The attack ends by enveloping the target in black, unquenchable fire.

rites.name: Teliaria
rites.text: A practitioner charges an opponent with blinding speed, striking from several angles with energy-infused fists. The final blow is swapped for a crackling lightning-thrust that ends the assault.

rites.name: Valontia
rites.text: A rare craft passed down only within one ancient lineage, letting its wielders command every basic element and two opposing forces. Its greatest forms are gathered by consuming a sacred fruit that holds the life of an entire world.

rites.name: Coronia Corenintia
rites.text: A wielder traps a foe inside a crushing orb of drawn-together stone, then drops it from the heavens. Charged with lightning, the wielder strikes the falling mass, unleashing a blast of storm-fire visible across the void.

rites.name: Sariasia
rites.text: A living energy found in the bodies of beings on some worlds, said to flow through all things and link every mind from its beginning. Gathering it can yield a potent fruit, and freeing it blends the body's physical and spiritual forces.

rites.name: Cistor
rites.text: A bearer lets a brilliant blue sigil flare, slipping back a few heartbeats of time to avoid an incoming blow. Repeated use grants a glimpse of coming moments, though the bearer lives through longer stretches than those around them.

rites.name: Salus
rites.text: A bearer fuses a gathered sphere of raw power with a howling wind-edged spin and hurls it at a foe. The blast is far greater than a normal strike and can shatter several floating worldlets at once.

rites.name: Leonanum
rites.text: A combined hurling-sphere technique formed by nine spinning orbs, each carrying a different primal force. Their simultaneous impact breaks apart a towering, shape-shifting foe and prevents her from keeping her form.

rites.name: Naulianus
rites.text: A fighter first strikes a foe with a gust that hurls them skyward, then calls forth a colossal spinning blade of wind surrounded by four orbiting spheres of raw power. Upon impact the whole assembly detonates into a vast dome of glowing energy.

rites.name: Sirnanes
rites.text: A practitioner dissolves their whole body into liquid and reforms at will, slipping through tiny gaps. Entering another's mouth lets them take over that body, but sudden sparks and disruption of their inner energy can undo the form.

rites.name: Serarnes
rites.text: A discipline of technique that lets its practitioners bend the fabric of distance and moment. It is a craft wielded by those who learn to reshape the flow of place and time.

rites.name: Ukavamraum
rites.text: Ukavamraum is a pair of jointed fulcrum-staves, each grip sculpted into a coiled serpent with scale-ridges and a carved head at the base, bound together by a braided tether that hums when stretched. It belongs to the Ki realm of the Ukaraeno universe, where the staves store and redirect ambient life-force. Its wielders describe it as a weapon that remembers every hand that has held it.
